signals.topic: ThinkingBlock SSE 事件类型映射缺失导致前端无法渲染思考内容
signals.summary: ContentBlock 到 SSE 事件映射逻辑中 ThinkingBlock 未被映射为 thinking_block 事件类型，前端无法接收到思考内容，用户无法在流式输出中看到 agent 的思考过程。
signals.review_reason: ThinkingBlock 映射缺失直接影响用户体验（看不到 agent 思考过程），但目前仅在 Hypothesis 属性测试边界场景下暴露（空 toolkit、thinking block），尚未有大范围用户投诉证据，降级为 P2。

source_issues.title: test: Hypothesis 属性测试发现 toolkit schema 和 SSE 事件映射边界 bug（2 个失败）
source_issues.evidence: ThinkingBlock(type='thinking') 期望映射到 'thinking_block' SSE 事件，实际返回空列表；前端将无法渲染 agent 的思考内容。

signals.topic: BaseDb subclass overrides drop kwargs causing AgentOS Memory Topics 500 errors
signals.summary: SqliteDb, AsyncSqliteDb, and RedisDb subclasses override BaseDb methods but drop kwargs (user_id, filter_expr, etc.) that the AgentOS router relies on per the BaseDb contract. This causes TypeError and 500 responses on the os.agno.com Memory > Topics view and other AgentOS endpoints.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: confirmed TypeError → 500 on the AgentOS Memory > Topics endpoint (a core hosted UI view), caused by 13 method signature drifts across all 3 supported database backends. This is a systemic contract violation in the database abstraction layer that surfaces in production on the main AgentOS dashboard.

source_issues.title: BaseDb subclass overrides drop kwargs declared by BaseDb
source_issues.evidence: 13 methods drift across SqliteDb, AsyncSqliteDb, and RedisDb. User hit 500 on GET /a2a/memory_topics with 'SqliteDb.get_all_memory_topics() got an unexpected keyword argument user_id'. Reproduced via inspect.signature diff. Affects the hosted os.agno.com Memory > Topics view and any custom agent using db.get_trace(session_id=...), db.get_traces(filter_expr=...) against non-default backends.

signals.topic: PIIDetectionGuardrail crashes on raw regex string input
signals.summary: PIIDetectionGuardrail's custom_patterns parameter does not accept raw regex strings. When users pass a plain string pattern (a natural usage pattern per the docs), the code calls pattern.search() on a str object and crashes with AttributeError. The fix would be to internally compile string patterns.
aliases: AttributeError str object has no attribute search
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation + security control failure: users following the documented API naturally pass raw regex strings and get a crash. PII detection guardrails are used for security-sensitive content — failure here means PII may pass through without being caught, silently defeating a security control. The crash is clear and reproducible.

source_issues.title: [Bug] custom_patterns in PIIDetectionGuardrail does not accept raw regex strings
source_issues.evidence: Users following the documented API pass raw regex strings and get 'AttributeError: str object has no attribute search'. PII detection is a security control — crash means PII is silently uncaught rather than flagged. Reproduced on agno 2.5.16 / Python 3.12.12.

signals.topic: Knowledge._update_content silently skips persistence when content row is missing
signals.summary: Knowledge._update_content and _aupdate_content bail with a warning log when the content row does not exist, instead of letting the backend upsert create it. Users get no error indicating their knowledge content was not saved, resulting in silent data loss.
aliases: Knowledge upsert bails on missing row
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss: knowledge content is never persisted when the row doesn't exist, yet no error or exception is raised — users receive no signal that their data was lost. This is a clear data integrity failure in a core knowledge management feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug] knowledge _update_content silently bails when content row missing
source_issues.evidence: When Content id does not exist in the contents table, both _update_content and _aupdate_content log a warning and return None without writing any row. Backend upsert capability is bypassed. No error is raised, so callers have no indication the content was not persisted.

signals.topic: AgentOS API exposes system prompts, model config, tools, and tool call results to all API clients
signals.summary: GET /agents and SSE run streams expose sensitive agent internals (full system prompts, model IDs/providers, tool configurations, raw tool inputs/outputs) to any API client with no opt-out mechanism. No server-side control exists to suppress these fields.
aliases: system prompt exposed to API clients
signals.review_reason: Critical data confidentiality breach in production: system prompts often contain proprietary business logic, data access rules, and confidential context exposed to any API client. Tool inputs/outputs streamed to frontend may leak data the user is not authorized to see. The only available workaround (stream_events=False) breaks progress indicators entirely, leaving no viable production path without custom middleware.

source_issues.title: [Security] AgentOS exposes sensitive agent internals to API clients — system prompt, model config, tools, and tool call results
source_issues.evidence: AgentResponse.from_agent() unconditionally includes system_message.instructions (full system prompt), model config, tools list. SSE ToolCallCompleted events stream raw tool_args and results to frontend with no way to suppress them without breaking UX (the only option stream_events=False suppresses all events). No server-side mechanism to restrict this data.

signals.topic: OutputCheckError raised in output_validation_post_hook is caught internally instead of propagating to caller
signals.summary: The OutputCheckError raised inside output_validation_post_hook is caught by the framework and logged as ERROR while the response is still returned normally. The documented try/except OutputCheckError pattern shown in the official docs is completely ineffective.
signals.review_reason: Contract violation of documented API: the official docs explicitly show OutputCheckError being raised to caller for retry handling, but the actual runtime catches it internally and returns the response normally. This makes the entire output validation hook pattern unreliable — users cannot trust their validation logic to trigger the documented error handling flow.

source_issues.title: [Bug] OutputCheckError not raised to caller in post-hook output validation — caught internally and logged instead
source_issues.evidence: The official documentation shows a try/except OutputCheckError pattern for retry/handling. In practice the exception is caught internally and logged as 'ERROR Validation failed: ...', the response is still returned to caller, and the except block is never reached. Contract violation of documented API behavior.

signals.topic: Thinking mode causes API 400 errors due to missing reasoning_content
signals.summary: When using thinking/reasoning-enabled models (kimi-2.6, deepseek-v4-pro), OpenCode fails to include reasoning_content in the assistant tool call message, causing the provider to return 400 errors and blocking the entire tool usage flow.
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked: thinking-enabled models (kimi-2.6, deepseek-v4-pro) return 400 errors and cannot perform tool calls, directly preventing users from completing any coding tasks. Multiple providers affected, hard to reproduce but confirmed by user evidence.

source_issues.title: thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is missing in assistant tool call message at index ...
source_issues.evidence: User reports 400 errors from both kimi-2.6 and deepseek-v4-pro providers when thinking mode is enabled: 'thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is missing in assistant tool call message at index 13' and 'reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API'. Session is blocked for any task requiring tool use with these models.

signals.topic: OpenAI 4xx errors display raw JSON body instead of human-readable error.message
signals.summary: OpenAI 4xx API errors render the raw JSON response body to users instead of extracting the inner error.message field, giving users no actionable hint and causing them to retry the same broken model selection multiple times.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is directly blocked by uninformative errors: users cannot diagnose why their model selection failed and retry the same broken operation repeatedly (3+ times documented), wasting API quota and time. Root cause is precisely identified in code.

source_issues.title: OpenAI 4xx errors render the raw response body instead of the inner error.message
source_issues.evidence: User sees 'APIError: Bad Request: {"error":{"message":"The model `gpt-5-codex` does not exist...'}}' instead of actionable text. Root cause identified in error.ts line 67: body.error object is truthy but not a string, short-circuiting the string extraction chain. Report documents users retrying the same broken model 3+ times because error gave no actionable hint.

signals.topic: Config file changes not detected or reloaded without restart
signals.summary: Modifications to opencode.json (both global and project-level) are not detected by OpenCode; the config cache persists from startup and ignores file changes, forcing users to manually restart or clear cache.
signals.review_reason: Significant workflow disruption: config changes are silently ignored, forcing developers into manual restart cycles. This breaks iterative development workflows and causes inconsistent behavior. While not a crash, it directly undermines the development experience and wastes developer time.

source_issues.title: Bug: Config Cache Not Updating After Changes to opencode.json
source_issues.evidence: User reports that changes to opencode.json are completely ignored until restart. Impact documented: 'Makes configuration updates ineffective, causes inconsistent behavior during development, forces manual restarts or cache clearing.' Critical for workflows where config is dynamically updated or generated.

signals.topic: Authentication header missing after restarting opencode, blocking tool use
signals.summary: After authenticating once in headless mode, quitting and relaunching opencode results in a 'Missing Authentication header' error, even though the auth.json file is present. Users are blocked from using the tool after every restart.
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked: authentication fails on every app restart, preventing users from using the tool. The auth.json file exists but is not loaded correctly, requiring users to re-authenticate repeatedly. Clear authentication persistence bug.

source_issues.title: Missing Authentication header when I try to use open code
source_issues.evidence: User authenticates successfully via headless mode, then quits and relaunches opencode — gets 'Missing Authentication header' error despite auth.json being present at the expected location. This blocks the user from using the tool after every restart.

signals.topic: OpenCode Desktop ignores user PATH, breaking MCP server startup
signals.summary: OpenCode Desktop (deb package) does not inherit the user's full PATH environment, causing MCP servers that depend on user-installed tools (npx, uvx) to fail with 'Executable not found in $PATH'. TUI works correctly with the same config.
aliases: MCP servers fail in desktop app
signals.review_reason: Key functionality completely broken in Desktop mode: all MCP servers that use user-installed tools (npx, uvx) fail to start. This affects core integrations (memory, filesystem, git MCP servers). The same config works in TUI, confirming Desktop has a PATH inheritance bug. Users relying on Desktop GUI are blocked from using MCP functionality.

source_issues.title: OpenCode Desktop ignores path, while TUI doesn't
source_issues.evidence: Desktop logs show 'Executable not found in $PATH: npx' and 'Executable not found in $PATH: uvx' while TUI with identical config works fine. User has npx at ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/lts/bin/npx — Desktop spawns sidecar with incomplete PATH, breaking all MCP servers that depend on user-installed tools.

signals.topic: embedded reflect.Type in API struct breaks Go linker dead-code elimination, causing larger binaries
signals.summary: The SDK embeds reflect.Type in its API struct, which causes Go's linker dead-code elimination to be disabled for all projects using the SDK. This results in significantly larger binary sizes and prevents build-time optimization.
aliases: dead code elimination disabled by SDK
large binary size due to reflect.Type embedding
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point with explicit user impact evidence: the user reports that using the SDK 'disabled dead code elimination on our projects', which directly causes larger binary sizes and prevents Go build optimization. The issue is confirmed by maintainers and cross-referenced with a similar known issue in openai/openai-go. The user is blocked from using standard Go build optimizations, which is a measurable cost (binary bloat) and affects all users of the SDK.

source_issues.title: bug: embedded reflect.Type breaks Go linker dead-code elimination
source_issues.evidence: Issue author explicitly states 'using this SDK disabled dead code elimination on our projects'. This is a verified and closed issue where a user (ofek-frame) reports that embedding reflect.Type in the SDK struct causes Go linker DCE to fail, leading to larger binaries. The issue is confirmed by maintainers and cross-referenced with openai/openai-go#609 which has the same root cause.

signals.topic: Java quickstart documentation uses non-existent Maven version and missing classpath setup, blocking new users from completing the get-started flow
signals.summary: The Java quickstart docs reference Maven version 2.20.0 which does not exist on Maven Central (404), and the javac/java command instructions lack the necessary classpath setup for the SDK JAR dependencies, causing immediate compilation failures for new users.
aliases: Java get started documentation wrong version
signals.review_reason: This is a clear first-time user onboarding blocker: the Maven version 404 means any new user following the official docs cannot resolve dependencies at all, and the missing classpath instructions mean javac/java compilation fails immediately. Both issues directly prevent users from completing the get-started flow.

source_issues.title: Java quickstart docs: javac/java commands don't work without classpath setup, version 2.20.0 doesn't exist
source_issues.evidence: Version 2.20.0 returns 404 from Maven Central. javac/java commands fail immediately because QuickStart.java imports com.anthropic.* JARs that javac has no knowledge of. The correct Maven approach (mvn compile exec:java) is not mentioned.

signals.topic: Structured output schema generator ignores Java nullability annotations, marking all fields as required and causing LLMs to hallucinate values
signals.summary: When using outputConfig with a Java class or record, the SDK's internal schema generator treats all fields as mandatory in the JSON Schema required array, ignoring @Nullable annotations and Optional types. This forces the LLM to hallucinate placeholder values (e.g., 'null' strings, empty strings, dashes) even when the user intends fields to be optional.
aliases: structured output required fields all mandatory
JSON schema generation ignores Java nullability
signals.review_reason: This is a real functional bug in a key feature (structured output): the schema generator incorrectly marks all fields required regardless of nullability intent, causing LLM to produce nonsensical hallucinated values in structured responses. The user's debugger evidence confirms the incorrect schema output.

source_issues.title: Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: Debugger inspection confirms every field (including @Nullable and Optional<String> fields) appears in the required array. LLM is forced to hallucinate values like 'null', empty string, or dash to satisfy schema. Attempted fixes with @Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and Optional type all fail.

signals.topic: Files API 累积孤立文件无法清理 — skill 与 file 关联字段缺失
signals.summary: Files API 不暴露 skill→file 关联信息，删除 skill 后底层文件变为孤立文件无法安全删除，导致账户上孤立文件无限累积且无法识别。
aliases: Files API orphan files cannot be cleaned up
无法清理 Files API 孤立文件
signals.review_reason: 该问题具有极强的用户影响证据：用户账户已有约 1100 个孤立文件持续累积，每次重新配置 skill 都会新增孤立文件，导致存储成本持续增长且无任何安全清理手段；同时 beta.skills.list 的分页上限 bug（cap at 100）进一步叠加了该问题，使其成为主流程阻断性问题（无法枚举账户全部 skills，无法构建文件→skill 逆向索引）。虽然 count=1 但 review_reason 明确给出了强用户影响证据，且为 beta 功能中的严重维护/成本问题，符合保留条件。

source_issues.title: Cannot GC orphan Files API files — skill→file linkage not exposed on skills.versions.retrieve
source_issues.evidence: 用户账户已有约 1100 个文件，其中没有任何文件可以安全识别为「孤立」或「被引用」状态；删除 skill 后文件仍在账户上无法清理；beta.files.list 缺少 after_id 分页或 scope/source_skill_id 过滤能力；beta.skills.list 有额外分页 bug（上限 100 条且 has_more=False 无法继续翻页），进一步加剧无法枚举所有 skill 的问题。

signals.topic: AsyncAnthropicVertex 在 US/EU region 下流式接口返回 404 阻断异步主流程
signals.summary: AsyncAnthropicVertex 在 region='us' 或 'eu' 时调用流式接口（streamRawPredict/rawPredict）得到 404，同步版本 AnthropicVertex 无此问题，导致异步用户无法使用美国和欧洲区域。
aliases: Async Vertex AI 404 in US/EU regions
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断性明确：异步 SDK 在美国和欧洲 region 下完全不可用（流式接口返回 404），而同步版本正常工作，属于 async/sync 行为不一致导致的阻断性问题。用户已有明确复现步骤和 HTTP 日志证据。count=1 但影响区域明确为北美的 US 和欧盟用户主流程，因单仓 count=1 降为 P1 而非 P0。

source_issues.title: Async methods NOT working with US/EU regions on Vertex AI - Gets 404 on endpoints
source_issues.evidence: 复现路径清晰：同步版本发送请求到 https://aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com/... (200 OK)；异步版本发送请求到 https://us-aiplatform.googleapis.com/... (404 Not Found)；仅在 region='us' 或 'eu' 时触发，region='global' 正常；已由用户确认代码级别差异。

signals.topic: Bedrock 流式 SSE 错误事件触发未捕获 ValueError 而非用户级 APIStatusError
signals.summary: Bedrock 流式接口返回错误 SSE 事件时 SDK 抛出未捕获的 ValueError，程序直接崩溃，而非向用户暴露可捕获的 APIStatusError，导致流式管道断裂。
aliases: SSE error event not handled gracefully
signals.review_reason: 流式管道异常处理不当：Bedrock 返回错误 SSE 事件时抛出未捕获 ValueError 导致程序崩溃，属于非预期错误处理路径；虽然阻断但仅影响 Bedrock 流式用户（count=1，单仓），且有其他错误处理路径的替代期望（APIStatusError），符合 P2 定位。

source_issues.title: Bedrock streaming SSE events errors are not handled gracefully
source_issues.evidence: 完整堆栈跟踪显示错误从 aiter_bytes → _parse_message_from_event → raise ValueError 全程向上传播未被捕获，程序以未处理异常退出；用户期望 SDK 内部重试或转换为 APIStatusError 供调用方处理。

signals.topic: 结构化输出功能对中等复杂度 JSON Schema 触发「compiled grammar too large」错误阻断采用
signals.summary: 使用 output_config.format + json_schema 时，常见的中等复杂度 JSON Schema（如嵌套 5 层、50 个属性、含 nullable 类型）会触发 400 错误并阻断结构化输出功能，用户被迫回退到 prompt-based JSON 指令失去格式保证。
aliases: JSON Schema complexity limit blocks structured outputs
结构化输出 grammar 过大错误
signals.review_reason: 核心功能采用阻断：结构化输出是官方 GA 功能，但中等复杂度的常见 Schema（5 层嵌套、nullable 类型、$ref/$defs）直接触发 400 阻断；用户被迫降级使用非保证格式的 prompt 注入；文档缺乏透明度（无实际限制说明）；属于功能可用性与文档完备性问题，count=1 单仓，P2。

source_issues.title: Structured outputs: compiled grammar is too large error needs better documentation and higher limits
source_issues.evidence: 用户已构建代码生成服务需返回复杂结构化数据，Schema 嵌套 5 层约 50 个属性属于 JSON Schema 常见模式但被拒绝；用户被迫放弃结构化输出的格式保证改用 prompt 注入 JSON；错误信息误导（提示减少 strict tools 但用户用的是 output_config.format 而非 tools）；文档未说明实际限制（属性数、嵌套深度、分支因子）。

signals.topic: beta.skills.list 分页上限固定为 100 且 has_more=False 导致大型账户无法枚举全部 skills
signals.summary: beta.skills.list 在账户拥有超过 100 个 skills 时返回 has_more=False 且无可用游标，阻止用户枚举完整技能列表，与孤立文件清理问题相互叠加。

signals.review_reason: 分页上限 bug 阻止枚举大型账户的完整 skills 列表，属于 beta API 可用性问题，与孤立文件清理问题相互关联；count=1 单仓，P2。

source_issues.evidence: 用户账户拥有超过 100 个 skills，调用 beta.skills.list 返回 has_more=False 但无 after_id 或 cursor 可用，无法枚举全部 skills，导致无法构建 skill→file 逆向索引来清理孤立文件。

signals.topic: TypeScript build breaks in v0.91.1 due to broken @ts-ignore in dist files
signals.summary: After v0.91.1 began formatting dist/* files with stainless-app, the @ts-ignore comments became block comments instead of line comments, causing TypeScript to fail compilation with 'Cannot find module' errors on undici-types relative path imports.
signals.review_reason: Release change (dist file formatting) directly causes TypeScript compilation failure for users upgrading to v0.91.1. Though only 1 issue, impact is explicit (blocks main build flow) with concrete TS error messages and a reproducible version. Meets pain point criteria of main flow blockage and significant experience degradation.

source_issues.title: Bug: Broken dist @ts-ignore in v0.91.1
source_issues.evidence: TypeScript compilation error: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/internal/types.d.ts:48:181 - error TS2307: Cannot find module '../../../node_modules/undici-types/index.d.ts'. Users upgrading to v0.91.1 encounter immediate build failures due to stainless-app formatting changing comment syntax from line to block comments.

signals.topic: MCP server unreachability causes entire request to fail atomically with no optional flag or actionable error
signals.summary: When any single injected MCP server is unreachable, the entire Messages API request fails with HTTP 400 and a generic error message that does not identify which server failed. No per-server timeout or optional flag exists, making multi-server production deployments fragile against any single server outage.
aliases: MCP server single point of failure
no graceful degradation for unreachable MCP servers
signals.review_reason: Single issue but with clear user impact: main flow blocked by single-server unreachability, and error message is non-actionable preventing reliable client-side recovery. User provides thorough root cause analysis with 5-dimensional failure space reasoning explaining why this is an API-layer problem. count=1 so P2 is appropriate; reviewed as P2 rather than P0 per priority rules.

source_issues.title: API: mcp_servers[].optional flag + structured error for graceful degradation on unreachable injected MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: User reports entire request fails atomically when one of multiple MCP servers is unreachable (e.g. transient tunnel or Cloudflare outage). The healthy server is never reached. Error message is non-actionable (no server name, format not contractual). Client-side workarounds are fundamentally unreliable per user's detailed 5-reason analysis covering SSRF, DNS rebinding, false negatives, race conditions, and non-contractual error parsing.

signals.topic: BaseExceptionGroup[CancelledError] escapes subprocess transport close() on second query() call in same event loop, crashing the caller
signals.summary: suppress(Exception) in SubprocessCLITransport.close() misses BaseExceptionGroup carrying CancelledError, causing a hard crash on every second query() call in the same event loop — deterministic and reproducible.
signals.review_reason: Deterministic crash on the second query() call is a main-flow blocking defect for any user running multiple queries in the same event loop (which is the documented async usage pattern). The BaseExceptionGroup escape causes a hard crash that terminates the caller's coroutine. This is not edge-case: it fires on the second call every time, making it effectively a guaranteed failure for the SDK's core async usage pattern.

source_issues.title: BaseExceptionGroup escapes transport.close() on second query() in the same event loop
source_issues.evidence: Second query() call in same asyncio event loop raises BaseExceptionGroup[CancelledError] from SubprocessCLITransport.close() due to suppress(Exception) not catching BaseExceptionGroup. Full repro script provided; crash is deterministic on every second query.

signals.topic: API-key users silently billed at 5-minute prompt cache TTL instead of 1-hour TTL due to bundled CLI version lag
signals.summary: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var (required to opt into 1-hour cache TTL) is absent from the bundled CLI version in SDK releases, causing months of compounding cost overpayment for all API-key users in production.
aliases: 5m cache TTL silently applied instead of 1h
prompt caching cost overcharge bundled CLI lag
signals.review_reason: Months of compounding financial damage across all API-key users in production, with explicit attribution to an SDK bundling defect (bundled CLI predates a required env var). This is cost-loss per unit of work that scales with session duration — the SDK's primary workload. User provided paid-billing evidence showing zero 1-hour cache hits despite the env var being set. This is a direct, quantifiable monetary loss, not an edge-case crash.

source_issues.title: API-key users silently stuck on 5m cache TTL: bundled CLI in v0.1.59 predates ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H opt-in
source_issues.evidence: User documents 8 months of production use with hundreds of thousands of agent turns all billed at the 5-minute tier. Concrete cache creation metrics show 4133 units at 5m vs 0 at 1h even when ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 is set. No SDK release has been tagged bundling CLI >= 2.1.108 where the env var was added. Anthropic developer relations publicly stated SDK customers get automatic cache savings, which is demonstrably false for API-key users.

signals.topic: MCP server tools fail to register on Windows (stdio transport): tools return 'No such tool available' despite server instructions visible in agent context
signals.summary: On Windows, MCP servers configured via mcp_servers={} with stdio transport spawn successfully but none of their tools are callable — every tool call returns 'No such tool available'. 100% reproducible, blocks all agentic workflows depending on stdio MCP servers on Windows.
aliases: Windows MCP stdio tools not callable
signals.review_reason: Full workflow blocking for Windows users who depend on stdio MCP servers (the most common MCP transport). The failure is 100% reproducible, confirmed by the agent itself in its diagnostic message, and all user-level workarounds fail. The MCP server binary itself works correctly when run outside the SDK, isolating the defect to the SDK's Windows stdio injection path.

source_issues.title: MCP server tools fail to register on Windows: server config visible to agent but tools return 'No such tool available'
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible across ~6 attempts on Windows 11 + Python 3.14. The MCP server's instructions appear in the agent context (confirming the server is 'connected') but none of its tools are callable. The author provides full repro config and a diagnostic message from the agent confirming the disconnect. All attempted workarounds (CLI version pin, env passthrough, settings.json, path changes) failed. Same code worked on 2026-04-30 morning with no code changes since.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport stderr anyio task group leaks cancel scope on normal query() completion, causing CPU spin
signals.summary: The anyio.create_task_group() used for stderr reading in SubprocessCLITransport has cross-task cancel scope affinity, causing the caller's task to be cancelled from an asyncgen finalizer on every normal query() completion. This pins one CPU core at 100% per completed query until process restart.
aliases: stderr task group cancel scope leak
signals.review_reason: CPU spin at 100% per completed query causes resource exhaustion on long-running SDK processes (common for the SDK's primary use case of long agent sessions). The defect fires deterministically on every normal query() completion using the documented API, not an edge case. Accumulation of stuck cancel scopes makes the process progressively worse over time.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Fires on every normal completion of async for message in query(...), which is the documented primary usage pattern. User provides CPU profiling evidence (100%+ on one core per completion) and full task/traceback evidence of cross-task cancel scope exit. Fix applied downstream as a subclass verified to eliminate CPU spin across 4+ consecutive completions. Same root cause as previously fixed bugs #454 and #776 in other files.

signals.topic: ProcessError(exit_code, stderr) stripped to generic Exception during error propagation — users cannot catch structured subprocess errors
signals.summary: When CLI subprocess exits non-zero, the original ProcessError with structured exit_code and stderr fields is destroyed through three propagation steps and re-raised as a bare Exception with a hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder. Users cannot programmatically handle CLI failures, retrieve exit codes, or associate stderr with specific failed calls in concurrent setups.
signals.review_reason: Broken error handling blocks users from writing programmatic failure recovery in concurrent and CI environments. The documented pattern try/except ProcessError does not work because the type is destroyed during propagation. This is a systematic SDK contract violation affecting any user who encounters a CLI subprocess failure — which is a common occurrence during development and production runs.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Verified repro showing isinstance(exc, ProcessError) is False and exc.stderr is absent after catching a CLI failure. Defect is a triple failure across subprocess_cli.py (hard-coded stderr literal), query.py message reader (str(e) destroys structured fields), and receive_messages (bare Exception re-raised). User documents three prior closed issues (#515, #282, #238) all hitting variants of the same problem.

signals.topic: Cache creation tokens charged on every turn even for byte-stable content, causing predictable cost leak
signals.summary: The SDK marks ~65K tokens as cache_create on every turn regardless of whether content changed, even when cache_read is accumulating correctly. This produces a persistent per-turn floor cost of $0.50-$0.65 that should be cache_read at 0.1x rate. Users report ~$175/day fleet-wide waste (~5K/month) with no workaround.
aliases: cache cost floor on null-content turns
signals.review_reason: Clear and quantified financial impact: ~$175/day fleet-wide cost leak. The cache_read accumulating correctly proves the prefix is already cached, confirming the cache_create floor is a redundant write. No workaround exists — users cannot inspect or control the cache breakpoint placement. This is a direct cost loss on every API call.

source_issues.title: cache issues in sdk
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction data shows ~65K cache_create per turn even on null-content turns (Turn 2/3 with only 'ok thanks'). cache_read accumulates correctly (+125K/turn) proving prefix IS cached, yet SDK rewrites ~65K fresh each turn. Cost impact: $0.50-0.65/turn * 50 turns/day * 35 agents = ~$175/day fleet-wide attributable to this floor.

signals.topic: beta.sessions events.stream() consistently fails for multi-session setups — 4 of 5 streams terminate before producing any event
signals.summary: Firing multiple beta.sessions.events.stream() calls (even serially, one at a time) causes 4 of 5 streams to crash with 'stream error: terminated' before any event arrives. The standard Messages API works reliably with identical auth/prompt/model. No HTTP errors or rate limits. Workaround is to use client.messages.create instead, but that defeats the sessions API purpose.
signals.review_reason: Primary workflow for beta.sessions is broken — 80% stream failure rate even in serial execution. The standard Messages API working in the same environment proves this is a sessions-API-specific defect, not an auth or quota issue. Users have no viable workaround within the sessions API and must fall back to client.messages.create, abandoning sessions functionality.

source_issues.title: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel (and serial) sessions fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events
source_issues.evidence: Multiple attempts across 5 runs: parallel attempts yield 1/5 success; serial attempt (1 at a time) also yields 1/5. Rules out concurrency ceiling. sawAnyEvent=false on all failures — stream never produced a single chunk. Standard Messages API (client.messages.create) works with same auth/key in same environment, confirming isolation to beta.sessions lifecycle.

signals.topic: SDK crashes with TypeError null-dereference when using outputFormat:json_schema in query()
signals.summary: A minimal query() call with outputFormat:{type:'json_schema',schema:{type:'object'}} crashes with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading effortLevel)' inside the SDK before any output is returned. The error surfaces as result.subtype:'error_during_execution' with no structured output. The root cause is an unguarded null return from an internal effort-resolution helper function (UT2() can return null). The same crash appears across multiple SDK versions.
signals.review_reason: Deterministic internal crash (not user-facing contract error) that renders structured output via json_schema completely unusable on affected SDK versions. The crash is inside SDK code before any output, so callers cannot handle or diagnose it. Cross-version regression suggests the bug has existed for multiple releases without fix.

source_issues.title: query() with minimal outputFormat: json_schema can crash internally with Cannot read properties of null (reading effortLevel)
source_issues.evidence: Minimal 25-line repro deterministically triggers crash. Error: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading effortLevel)' inside SDK. Internal helper UT2() returns null for this code path. No structured output returned; result.subtype='error_during_execution'. Confirmed across multiple older SDK versions (not a recent regression).

signals.topic: SDK runtime platform detection selects wrong libc binary on Debian arm64 (musl vs glibc mismatch)
signals.summary: On node:22-slim (Debian 12 aarch64/GLIBC), the SDK's runtime variant selector incorrectly picks the musl binary despite only the glibc binary being installed by npm. This is a regression from the v0.2.113 native-binary refactor — v0.2.76 worked fine in the same image. All query() calls fail immediately with a missing-binary error, completely blocking SDK usage in Docker/Kubernetes arm64 deployments.
signals.review_reason: Complete startup failure for SDK in a common deployment target (Debian arm64 Docker/Kubernetes). Regression from prior working version means existing deployments upgraded to 0.2.119 are broken. Marked duplicate confirms multiple users hitting the same issue.

source_issues.title: v0.2.119 picks linux-arm64-musl variant on Debian (glibc) arm64 even when only linux-arm64 is installed
source_issues.evidence: Docker repro confirms: npm installs 'claude-agent-sdk-linux-arm64' (glibc) correctly, but runtime selector requests 'claude-agent-sdk-linux-arm64-musl' which does not exist on disk. Error: 'Container exited with code 1: .../claude-agent-sdk-linux-arm64-musl/claude'. Regression from v0.2.76 (last known good). Blocks all query() usage in affected Docker/Kubernetes environments.

signals.topic: API returns 400 errors with empty body, blocking workflow with no diagnostic information
signals.summary: The API returns 400 status errors with no response body, blocking user conversations entirely. Errors occur repeatedly over ~1.5 hours (13 errors across multiple events). The error is marked canRetry:false, preventing automatic recovery. The message '0 tool calls, 0 tool results, 0 history entries' provides no actionable diagnostic information — users cannot determine if the cause is auth, rate limiting, or format.
signals.review_reason: Blocking workflow failures (canRetry:false) with no diagnostic information. The repeated nature over a session (13 errors/1.5h) and the inability to determine root cause (auth vs quota vs format) significantly degrades the user experience. The absence of retry makes recovery manual and disruptive.

source_issues.title: 400 status code (no body)
source_issues.evidence: 13 errors over ~1.5 hours from a long-lived agent. canRetry:false on all occurrences prevents automatic recovery. Error message provides no diagnostic detail: 'no body', 'no obvious shape problem'. No way for user to determine whether cause is auth, quota, or format. Blocks conversation entirely — user cannot continue work.

signals.topic: GitHub Copilot SWE agent actor triggers 404 crash in checkHumanActor, bypassing allowed_bots
signals.summary: When triggered by GitHub Copilot SWE agent, GITHUB_ACTOR is set to 'Copilot' (no [bot] suffix). The checkHumanActor function calls GET /users/Copilot which returns 404, crashing the action before allowed_bots logic is ever evaluated. Users with allowed_bots='*' are still blocked.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked — action exits with code 1 before any bot-allow logic runs. User has allowed_bots='*' configured yet Copilot SWE agent still fails. Clear 404 error with full logs demonstrates action is non-functional for this actor.

source_issues.title: Action fails with "Not Found" when triggered by GitHub Copilot (actor Copilot returns 404 from/users/ API)
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with exit code 1 before allowed_bots logic is consulted. GET /users/Copilot returns 404. Logs show 'Warning: SECURITY WARNING: Bypassing write permission check for Copilot' but action still crashes at the subsequent 404 call.

signals.topic: OAuth token fails validateHeaders after Pro→Max subscription upgrade, causing action to exit with SDK error
signals.summary: After upgrading from Pro to Max plan, the OAuth token (sk-ant-oat01-*) is no longer propagated to the Claude Code subprocess. The SDK init fails with 'Could not resolve authentication credentials' because both apiKey and authToken are null, despite the token being visible in the environment. API key workaround defeats the purpose of OAuth.
aliases: Pro to Max upgrade token broken
OAuth token null after subscription upgrade
signals.review_reason: OAuth-based authentication is completely broken post-Max upgrade for affected users. Main workflow fails with SDK execution error and exit code 1. The only workaround (API key) loses the subscription-tier benefit of OAuth tokens. Pre/post upgrade evidence clearly shows the upgrade as the trigger.

source_issues.title: Intermittent validateHeaders failure with Max-plan OAuth tokens after Pro→Max upgrade
source_issues.evidence: Action fails with 'Could not resolve authentication credentials' from SDK validateHeaders. Both apiKey and authToken are null in SDK init despite CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN being set. All workarounds tried (token regeneration, dual placement, credentials file pre-write) fail. Only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY workaround functions but defeats OAuth purpose. Same workflow worked reliably for weeks pre-upgrade.

signals.topic: Private/internal plugin marketplace repositories fail to clone due to missing git authentication in base-action
signals.summary: When using plugin_marketplaces with a private or internal GitHub repository, marketplace cloning fails with 'repository not found' (GitHub's auth-denied error) even though GITHUB_TOKEN is set and the GitHub App is installed on the marketplace repo. Root cause: configureGitAuth() is only called in agent/tag modes but not in base-action before installPlugins().
aliases: git auth not configured for marketplace
signals.review_reason: Private plugin marketplace functionality is completely non-functional for private/internal repos. The root cause is precisely identified (git auth not configured before marketplace install in base-action). Users must create extra PATs as workaround, reducing security. Key feature (private MCP marketplaces) is unavailable.

source_issues.title: Bug: Marketplace cloning fails with 'repository not found' for private/internal repos - git authentication not configured
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis provided: configureGitAuth() exists in src/github/operations/git-config.ts but is only called in agent/tag modes. Marketplace installation in base-action/src/index.ts happens before git auth is configured, causing 'HTTPS authentication failed / repository not found'. No workaround available without creating additional PATs.

signals.topic: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands causing turn exhaustion and job cancellation
signals.summary: The safety detector incorrectly flags valid bash commands as multiple operations: awk with && inside patterns, python3 -c inline strings, and file paths ending with '0:' (Windows drive letter false positive). Accumulated blocks cause Claude to exhaust all 80 turns and the job is cancelled.
aliases: turn exhaustion from false positive blocks
signals.review_reason: Multiple valid bash commands are incorrectly blocked by the multi-operation detector, leading to complete workflow failure (turn exhaustion + job cancellation). Three specific false-positive patterns documented with error messages. Impact is blocking despite single count, as the detector actively prevents legitimate workflows from completing.

source_issues.title: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk, python3 -c, Windows path pattern)
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct false positive patterns documented with exact error messages: (1) 'awk NR>=270 && NR<=310' blocked as multiple operations, (2) 'python3 -c' blocked as multiple operations, (3) paths ending in '0:' flagged as Windows drive letters. All three accumulate approval prompts until Claude exhausts 80 turns and job is cancelled with 'Error: The operation was canceled.' Consistent reproduction on GHES.

signals.topic: .claude-pr/ snapshot directory stealth-committed to user PR branches on bot fix-up commits
signals.summary: The .claude-pr/ directory created by restoreConfigFromBase is unintentionally committed to the user's PR branch when the bot pushes fix-up commits. The bot's reply comment only mentions the intended fix, leaving users unaware of the stealth chore commit that pollutes the PR with unrelated files. No mention in .gitignore, no mention in bot comment.
signals.review_reason: Action produces stealth commits to user repositories without any user-facing notification, violating the expected ephemeral nature of .claude-pr/ artifacts. The bot's reply comment misleads users about what was committed. This is a data-integrity concern: user's PR history is polluted without any indication. Suggested fix is clear and low-risk (git/info/exclude).

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase snapshot at .claude-pr/ gets committed to PR branch when bot pushes a fix
source_issues.evidence: Two real-world stealth commits documented: (1) chore commit adding ~100 files of .claude-pr/ snapshot on a hardware OEM PR unrelated to the commit content, (2) re-sync of .claude-pr/ on a subsequent fix-up. Bot's reply comment summarizes only the requested change, providing no signal about the .claude-pr/ commit. Requires manual git log review to discover. restoreConfigFromBase already git-resets SENSITIVE_PATHS but omits .claude-pr/ itself.

signals.topic: Desktop Code tab UI failures — Windows send button unresponsive and macOS Code tab missing despite confirmed seat upgrade
signals.summary: Code tab is completely non-functional for paying desktop app users on both Windows (send button fails on all inputs) and macOS (Code tab absent despite confirmed seat upgrade).
signals.review_reason: Code tab is completely non-functional for paying desktop app users. Windows: send button fails silently on all inputs (Enter, Ctrl+Enter, click) — confirmed has-repro with prior related issues. macOS: Code tab doesn't appear despite confirmed seat upgrade email and 20+ hours of waiting. These are separate issues but both result in complete inability to use the primary Claude Code interface in the desktop app.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Code tab send button completely unresponsive on Windows 11
source_issues.evidence: Send button does nothing on Enter, Ctrl+Enter, and click; Chat and Cowork tabs work; terminal works; only Code tab GUI broken; related issues #47320, #46937, #33771.

source_issues.title: Code tab not appearing in desktop app despite seat upgrade
source_issues.evidence: Received seat upgrade email confirming Claude Code access; Code tab does not appear in desktop app; tried reinstall, sign-out/in, waited 20+ hours; only Chat and Cowork tabs visible; user needs access for work urgently.

signals.topic: API ECONNRESET failures causing complete main workflow blockage
signals.summary: API becomes completely unavailable for extended periods (15+ hours) in long-context sessions, with all 10 retry attempts exhausted and no user actionable workaround.
signals.review_reason: API becomes completely unavailable for 15+ hours in long-context sessions. The retry mechanism exhausts all 10 attempts, leaving the user unable to work. Strong evidence this is server-side (errno:0 indicating HTTP/2 RST_STREAM, curl succeeding while SDK fails). Severity is unambiguous — complete workflow blockage for extended periods. Marked duplicate reduces frequency confidence but the user impact evidence is compelling.

source_issues.title: Persistent ECONNRESET (errno=0) on api.anthropic.com/v1/messages?beta=true — fails through all 10 retries
source_issues.evidence: 151 error events across 4 sessions over 12 days; session stayed broken for 15+ hours; 10/13 retry sequences exhausted all 10 retries; curl to same host succeeds while SDK fails; only one specific long-running session affected (132/151 errors).

signals.topic: Worktree isolation broken — subagent file writes commit to wrong branch instead of isolated worktree
signals.summary: The isolation:worktree feature is fundamentally broken; subagents write to absolute paths under the parent checkout instead of the worktree, then commit to main, defeating the entire purpose of worktree isolation for parallel audit/fix sweeps.
signals.review_reason: The isolation: worktree feature is fundamentally broken — subagents write to absolute paths under the parent checkout instead of the worktree, then commit to main. This defeats the entire purpose of worktree isolation for parallel audit/fix sweeps. Users experience 30+ minutes of merge conflict resolution per affected round, with orphaned duplicate commits in history. No viable workaround.

source_issues.title: isolation: "worktree" does not actually isolate subagent file writes
source_issues.evidence: Multiple concrete cases documented: Round 2 Group F all 3 fixes committed to main; Round 2 Group D committed to main with bundled WIP; Round 2 Group C committed once to main then again to worktree leaving duplicate; Round 1 all 4 fixes committed to main. Each round cost 30+ minutes of merge-conflict resolution.

signals.topic: Excessive token consumption on initial prompts and simple continuations causing direct monetary loss
signals.summary: Users on paid Opus 4.7 plans ($200/month) experiencing 38% session quota consumed on a single 'continue' prompt with no actual analysis performed, persisting for two weeks.
signals.review_reason: User on $200/month Opus 4.7 plan experiencing 38% session consumption on a single 'continue' with no actual analysis performed. This represents clear, direct monetary loss. The user explicitly identifies a token leak and has been experiencing this for two weeks. While not a workflow blocker, the financial impact on paying users is unambiguous.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Anthropic API: Excessive token consumption on initial prompt and simple continuations
source_issues.evidence: Single 'continue' prompt consumed 38% of session quota; paying $200 for Opus 4.7; problem persisting for 2 weeks; 2% per activity adds up quickly; user explicitly states 'there is definitely a leakage somewhere'.

signals.topic: /ultrareview burned free quota on server-side rate-limit failure instead of failing cleanly
signals.summary: Server-side rate-limit failures consume the user's free quota allocation without returning any useful results, losing the last free review opportunity with nothing to show.
aliases: free quota consumed on failed run
failed skill run still costs user
signals.review_reason: Server-side rate-limit failure consumed the user's last free quota allocation, leaving them unable to complete the review they needed. Failed runs should not consume limited free quota — this is a direct cost to the user caused by server-side failures outside their control. The user lost their final free review attempt with zero results.

source_issues.title: [BUG] /ultrareview burned free quota on server-side rate-limit failure
source_issues.evidence: Used last free run (3 of 3); got empty findings due to server rate limit; then got 'Extra Usage credits exhausted' on re-run; user lost free quota with nothing to show.

signals.topic: Telegram bot silently goes deaf mid-session — polling halts, no reconnect
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin can permanently stop polling for inbound updates while MCP server stays alive. Outbound calls work but the bot never receives messages. After MCP recycle (e.g., /mcp dialog or plugin re-auth), the bot does not auto-reconnect.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct Telegram issues both result in the bot going silently deaf mid-conversation. Users receive no indication the bot has stopped receiving messages. This is a critical reliability failure for the Telegram integration used as a primary communication channel.

source_issues.title: [telegram] MCP disconnects mid-session and does not auto-reconnect after /mcp dialog or other plugin re-auth
source_issues.evidence: Telegram plugin disconnects when MCP server processes are recycled. After disconnect, Telegram MCP does not come back automatically. User must run /reload-plugins to recover.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): retry polling on silent bot.start() resolution
source_issues.evidence: bot.start() resolves via paths other than bot.stop() under certain network conditions. When that happens, the return exits the polling-retry loop but stdin keeps process alive. Bot permanently goes deaf to inbound messages with no user notification.

signals.topic: ralph-loop unbounded iterations (max_iterations=0) — no safety net when model never emits <promise>
signals.summary: When ralph-loop is started with max_iterations=0 (unbounded), there is no backstop if the model never emits the configured <promise> tag. The loop can iterate thousands of times over many hours, burning compute with no user notification.
signals.review_reason: Two issues compound: (1) stop hook can intermittently miss the exit condition due to transcript flush race, (2) unbounded mode has no safety net. Real incident ran 6,239 iterations over 11.7 hours. This represents significant wasted compute cost and potential for runaway sessions.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: add safety net for runaway when promise never emitted
source_issues.evidence: max_iterations: 0 (unbounded mode) has no backstop if model never emits <promise>. Real incident ran 6,239 iterations over ~11.7 hours with no exit.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: stop hook intermittently misses <promise> tag due to transcript flush race (downstream of claude-code#15813)
source_issues.evidence: Stop hook reads JSONL transcript before Claude's final text block is finalized. Hook intermittently misses the <promise>...</promise> tag on the exit turn. Author observed race window directly with instrumentation trace.

signals.topic: TypeScript LSP server fails to start on Windows (ENOENT / libuv spawn error)
signals.summary: uv_spawn cannot find typescript-language-server on Windows because npm installs .cmd shims without .exe, and libuv requires shell:true or extension. The LSP server never starts, making the typescript-lsp plugin completely non-functional on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (typescript-lsp) is completely non-functional on Windows due to spawn failure. User's LSP workflow is blocked with ENOENT error. This is a mainflow failure for Windows users.

source_issues.title: typescript-lsp: ENOENT on Windows — libuv can't spawn typescript-language-server (.cmd shim, no .exe)
source_issues.evidence: npm installs typescript-language-server as .cmd/.ps1/.sh shims but no .exe. uv_spawn on Windows resolves via PATHEXT only if shell:true is passed. Spawn returns ENOENT even though command -v resolves. The LSP server never starts on Windows.

signals.topic: SessionStart hook fails on Windows — /usr/bin/bash is PE executable, not shell
signals.summary: The SessionStart hook uses /usr/bin/bash which on Windows resolves to a PE32+ executable that cannot be interpreted as a shell script. The hook fails to execute, breaking plugin initialization on Windows.
signals.review_reason: SessionStart hook is a core plugin initialization mechanism. It fails on every Windows session, preventing plugin hooks from running. This is a mainflow block for Windows users.

source_issues.title: SessionStart hook fails on Windows: /usr/bin/bash is PE executable, not shell
source_issues.evidence: On Windows with Git Bash, /usr/bin/bash resolves to C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe — a PE32+ Windows executable, not a Unix shell interpreter. Claude Code tries to execute the hook script and produces 'cannot execute binary file' error.

signals.topic: skill-creator run_loop fails completely on Windows (select.select on pipes + cp1252 encoding)
signals.summary: skill-creator's description-optimization loop fails for every Windows user due to two bugs: select.select on pipes is Windows-incompatible (WinError 10038), and Path.write_text defaults to cp1252 which cannot encode special characters like '✗'. The tool is unusable on Windows.
signals.review_reason: skill-creator is a core plugin used for building new skills. It fails completely for all Windows users with two distinct errors. This blocks the skill creation workflow entirely on Windows.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop fails on Windows (select.select on pipes + cp1252 encoding)
source_issues.evidence: select.select on pipes is Windows-incompatible (only works on sockets on Windows) causing WinError 10038. Path.write_text() defaults to platform encoding (cp1252 on Windows) which cannot encode '✗' character, causing UnicodeEncodeError. Both patches verified locally. Fails for every Windows user.

signals.topic: Plugin loader installs all repo skills instead of only skills declared in marketplace.json
signals.summary: When installing a plugin via /plugin install, the plugin loader caches the entire repository and loads ALL skills found in the skills/ directory, ignoring the `skills` array declared in marketplace.json. This causes namespace pollution — e.g., the document-skills plugin installs 17 skills instead of the declared 4.
aliases: plugin skill filter not respecting marketplace.json
plugin installer loads all skills from repo
signals.review_reason: This is a real functional bug in the plugin installation flow. The plugin loader's failure to respect the marketplace.json `skills` array causes incorrect behavior: users get a polluted skills namespace with 13 extra unintended skills. This breaks the advertised plugin installation contract and causes discoverability/confusion. Count=1 from a single repo, so P1 (not P0) but still a clear user-impacting bug.

source_issues.title: document-skills plugin loads all skills from repo instead of only declared ones in marketplace.json
source_issues.evidence: Installing document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills loads 17 skills instead of the 4 declared in marketplace.json. The cache directory contains all 17 skill folders and the plugin loader loads them all without filtering.

signals.topic: Desktop UI silently discards custom MCP extensions and environment variables on restart — config rollback breaks custom setups
signals.summary: Goose Desktop UI does not correctly persist custom MCP extension configuration. Environment variables set via the UI are ignored; manual YAML edits are silently rolled back on restart. Users report that MCP extensions configured through the UI fail to load with secrets missing errors, and manually edited config.yaml changes are lost.
aliases: MCP extension env vars not saved from Desktop UI
config rollback on restart wipes custom extensions
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports on Win11 and Windows 10 confirm the Desktop UI fails to persist MCP extension configuration (env vars + custom extensions). This is a multi-turn session state corruption issue: users set up custom extensions via the UI, only to find them wiped or broken after restart. The config self-check mechanism actively destroys user configuration.

source_issues.title: Silent Rollback of Manually Edited config.yaml on Restart Breaks Custom MCP Extensions
source_issues.evidence: Manually edited config.yaml changes are silently rolled back on restart. The configuration self-check mechanism on startup aggressively wipes non-built-in extensions. Custom MCP extensions fail to load.

source_issues.title: Win11 Goose desktop Extentsion(MCP): values of Environment Variables cannot be retrieved by system
source_issues.evidence: Environment Variables set via Desktop UI for MCP extensions are not being read by the system. Error: 'Failed to fetch secret JWT_TOKEN from config: Configuration value not found'. Values saved in config.yaml are empty. Manually hardcoding env vars in yaml works.

signals.topic: Streaming chunk parse error when tool_calls function arguments is null — blocks tool use for affected models
signals.summary: When LLM streaming responses include null `arguments` in `tool_calls[].function`, Goose fails to parse the chunk and the tool call chain breaks entirely. This is a streaming parse failure that silently blocks the agent from executing any downstream tools for models (e.g. deepseek-v4-pro) that emit null instead of absent/missing arguments.
aliases: tool_calls function arguments null parse failure
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine parse-time blocking bug: the agent loop cannot process streaming tool_calls when arguments is null, resulting in complete tool call failure. Users observe agent dead-ends and silent failures. While count=1, the impact is severe (full workflow block for any model emitting null), and the code path is a clear deserialize mismatch.

source_issues.title: Failed to parse streaming chunk: invalid type: null when llm response tool_calls function arguments is null
source_issues.evidence: Streaming chunk contains `{"function":{"arguments":null}}` which fails Rust deserialization. The `DeltaToolCallFunction` struct defines `name: Option<String>` but not `arguments: Option<String>`, causing parse failure on null. Agent workflow is blocked whenever affected model emits null arguments.

signals.topic: Goose Desktop in WSL hangs indefinitely during MCP OAuth/DCR authorization — app becomes unresponsive
signals.summary: When Goose Desktop runs inside WSL and encounters an MCP server requiring OAuth/DCR authorization, it cannot open a browser window for the authorization URL. The app hangs with no error message and becomes completely unresponsive to new queries, blocking the entire MCP extension registration workflow.
aliases: Desktop UI unresponsive during MCP OAuth
signals.review_reason: App-level hang that makes the entire conversation UI unresponsive is a critical workflow block. While count=1, the severity is high: the user cannot proceed with MCP server registration at all, and the hang manifests as 'loading conversation...' with no recovery path other than force-quit.

source_issues.title: Goose desktop in WSL hangs when registering a DCR MCP server
source_issues.evidence: In WSL environment, Goose Desktop attempts DCR authorization with an MCP server but cannot open the browser. The app hangs with 'loading conversation...' indefinitely and stops responding to new queries. The conversation is completely blocked.

signals.topic: Custom providers created via Desktop UI do not appear in the provider selector — files saved but UI registration fails silently
signals.summary: Custom provider JSON files are correctly written to disk by the Desktop UI, but the provider selector in Settings does not display them. This forces affected users to use the CLI as a workaround, creating an inconsistent experience between Desktop and CLI.
aliases: Custom provider JSON files not loaded into Desktop UI provider list
Desktop UI custom provider registration silent failure
signals.review_reason: A clear UI-to-state synchronization bug: the Desktop UI successfully writes provider JSON to disk but fails to register them in its own internal state, causing silent display failure. The workaround of using CLI is not acceptable for Desktop users. The evidence of duplicate JSON files confirms the UI is retrying and failing silently.

signals.topic: Extension Manager read_resource silently returns wrong extension data on URI collisions — errors swallowed across extensions
signals.summary: When multiple MCP extensions expose resources at the same URI, the Extension Manager's read_resource tool treats extension_name as optional and silently iterates all extensions, returning the first match with no error. The list_resources schema declares extension_name but the handler reads a different parameter name (extension), so explicit filtering calls are also silently ignored.
aliases: MCP resource URI collision silent failure
signals.review_reason: This is a silent data integrity failure: the model receives incorrect resource data from the wrong extension with no indication of ambiguity. The fan-out loop actively destroys error distinguishability (auth failures, transport errors, not-found). This is a structural design flaw, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: read_resource: optional extension_name causes silent probe-all across extensions
source_issues.evidence: With two or more resource-capable extensions exposing the same URI, read_resource silently returns whichever extension matches first by iteration order, swallowing all errors. list_resources declares extension_name in schema but the handler reads 'extension', so explicit filtering calls are silently ignored. Auth, transport, and not-found errors are all lost.

Multiple features interact (ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context), making this a non-obvious regression that likely affects any user combining these features.

signals.topic: result_as_answer=true causes agent to accept tool error outputs as valid final answers
signals.summary: When result_as_answer=True is set on a tool, the agent treats the tool's error output as its final answer regardless of whether the tool call succeeded or failed. This breaks agent reflection logic — error messages from failed tool executions (e.g., code execution failures) become the agent's answer instead of triggering retry or error handling.
signals.review_reason: This is a logic error that silently corrupts agent behavior — a tool's error output becomes the agent's final answer instead of triggering reflection or retry. The user explicitly identifies this as removing the agent's capability to reflect on its output. While the workflow may not crash, the semantic correctness of results is destroyed, which is a critical functional regression for any agent relying on result_as_answer with tools that can fail.

source_issues.title: [BUG] If result_as_answer=true is set, then irrespective of tool's failure or success, tool output which essentially is error returned will become final answer of agent
source_issues.evidence: User describes: 'Agent ignores the success of tool and make the tool output its own, which shouldn't happen. result_as_answer=True should work for only successful tool calls, This essentially removing the capability of agent reflecting on its output.' signals.topic: Codex model ignores instruction to never stop, breaking interactive sessions in autoresearch
signals.summary: The Codex model does not respect the 'never stop' instruction when used with autoresearch, causing premature termination of interactive agent sessions. Unlike Claude, Codex terminates mid-session, preventing users from observing agent progress and providing interactive input. This defeats the core value proposition of interactive sessions in autoresearch.
signals.review_reason: Codex prematurely terminates interactive sessions due to not respecting the 'never stop' instruction, which is a functional incompatibility that breaks the core interactive session workflow. Author (karpathy, the repo owner) confirms the issue. However, count=1 and only affects one model (Codex), so classified as P2 rather than P1. Keep=true because there is explicit user-reported evidence of workflow breakdown.

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.ls silently swallows FileNotFoundError/PermissionError, returning empty LsResult
signals.summary: BaseSandbox.ls catches FileNotFoundError and PermissionError with bare `pass`, returning LsResult(entries=[], error=None) — identical to a genuinely empty directory. Two independent reports confirm this. Agents cannot distinguish 'path does not exist' or 'permission denied' from 'empty directory', leading to poisoned context and wrong decisions.
aliases: ls returns empty for non-existent paths
ls silent failure on invalid paths
signals.review_reason: Two independent external users independently reported the same bug with full reproduction code. The bug causes a silent failure that makes agents unable to distinguish 'directory is empty' from 'path does not exist' or 'permission denied'. The agent proceeds with wrong assumptions, poisoning its reasoning context — a significant workflow-level failure. Classified as P1 (not P0) because count=2 across a single repo without a clear third independent report.

source_issues.title: fix(sdk): BaseSandbox.ls silently swallows FileNotFoundError/PermissionError, returning empty LsResult on invalid paths
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible bug with full Python example; BaseSandbox.ls returns LsResult(entries=[], error=None) for both non-existent paths and permission-denied directories; agent context is poisoned with false information; issue author explicitly states 'This causes my agent's context to be poisoned with false information, therefore not able to self-reflect properly'.

source_issues.title: fix(sdk): BaseSandbox.ls silently swallows FileNotFoundError/PermissionError, returning empty LsResult on invalid paths

signals.topic: IndexError crash in SubAgentMiddleware when LLM returns empty messages list
signals.summary: SubAgentMiddleware._run_subagent() crashes with IndexError at line 411 when accessing result['messages'][-1].text on an empty messages list returned by the LLM. Triggered by rate limits, timeouts, or models that return no content.
signals.review_reason: Hard crash (IndexError) in SubAgentMiddleware triggered by a legitimate LLM edge case (empty messages). The subagent workflow is completely blocked with no graceful degradation. Despite count=1, the severity warrants P1: every real-world deployment hitting rate limits or using models with edge-case behavior will encounter this. No workaround available to the user without patching the SDK.

source_issues.title: `IndexError` in `SubAgentMiddleware` when LLM returns empty messages

Reproduction: any scenario where LLM returns a valid response but with empty messages array (timeout, rate limit, model edge case). Subagent workflow is completely blocked — no graceful degradation, just a hard crash.

signals.topic: Virtual paths from CompositeBackend routes don't resolve in LocalShellBackend.execute, causing agent command failures and retry loops
signals.summary: CompositeBackend routes file operations by path prefix, but execute() always delegates to the default backend without path rewriting. When skills use virtual paths like /common/skills/yyy/xxx.py, execute() passes the literal path to the shell where it doesn't exist, causing command failures and agent retry loops.
aliases: execute() does not route virtual paths
skill execution fails with virtual filesystem paths
signals.review_reason: Concrete workflow-blocking bug: skills using virtual filesystem paths fail at the execute() step because LocalShellBackend.execute() receives untranslated paths. The agent enters a retry loop (ls/grep work, execute fails), wasting tokens and failing to complete tasks. Real operational impact in multi-backend setups. P1 despite count=1 due to complete workflow blockage in affected scenarios.

source_issues.title: Virtual paths from `CompositeBackend` routes don't resolve in `LocalShellBackend.execute`
source_issues.evidence: Agent skill execution fails because execute() doesn't rewrite virtual paths like file operations do. Shell receives literal /common/... path that doesn't exist on the host OS. Confirmed by source analysis: 'execution is not path-routable — it always delegates to the default backend.' The agent probes with ls/grep (which work correctly) but execute fails, producing a retry loop. No workaround without modifying SKILL.md.

signals.topic: langchain-deepseek: Multi-turn agent calls fail with 400 error due to missing reasoning_content passback
signals.summary: DeepSeek integration's _get_request_payload does not include reasoning_content from prior AI messages, causing DeepSeek API to return 400 errors on multi-turn conversations (2nd+ LLM call). Root cause: _convert_message_to_dict strips additional_kwargs including reasoning_content, and the passback logic is missing.
signals.review_reason: 4 duplicate issues with identical root cause. Multi-turn agent calls are a core workflow that gets completely blocked (400 API error) on the 2nd LLM turn. Explicit stack traces, reproduction code, and root cause analysis provided. Impacts deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-r1 models. This is a primary use-case failure (agent execution), not edge-case.

signals.topic: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware executes rejected tool calls in LangGraph ToolNode despite rejection decision
signals.summary: When HumanInTheLoopMiddleware receives a reject decision, it returns the tool_call in its output, leaving it in the AIMessage.tool_calls list. LangGraph's ToolNode then blindly executes the rejected tool, ignoring the rejection ToolMessage. The fix is returning (None, tool_message) on reject so ToolNode skips the tool.
signals.review_reason: Clear logical bug in a core security-critical workflow. When a human reviewer explicitly rejects a tool call, the tool is still executed by ToolNode. This violates the core safety guarantee of HumanInTheLoopMiddleware and can lead to unintended side effects from executing tools without human authorization. Reproduction code confirms the bug. Has associated fix PR.

source_issues.title: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware executes rejected tool calls in LangGraph's ToolNode
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction code with unittest.mock demonstrating assert len(updated_ai_message.tool_calls)==1 after rejection (bug: should be 0). Related PR #37092 already prepared with fix. Logical bug where security-critical human-in-the-loop approval is bypassed by automatic tool execution.

signals.review_reason: User-facing experience failure for anyone copying documentation examples. While only 1 issue, the impact is direct and common: docstring code examples are meant to be copy-pasted. The 404 error is immediate and blocks the example from running at all. Proposed fix is trivial (model name replacement).

source_issues.title: docs(core): retired `claude-2` model referenced in `RunnableWithMessageHistory` docstring examples
source_issues.evidence: Explicit error: anthropic.NotFoundError 404 'model: claude-2'. Two docstring examples (lines 138 and 191) affected. Users who copy-paste docstring code hit immediate API failure. Clear reproduction and proposed fix (replace with claude-sonnet-4).

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators use lexicographic comparison instead of numeric, causing incorrect query results
signals.summary: PostgresStore._get_filter_condition() uses text extraction (`value->>key`) and `str(value)` for $gt/$gte/$lt/$lte operators, causing numeric comparisons to use lexicographic ordering. A document with score=2 incorrectly passes a `{"score": {"$gte": 10}}` filter.
aliases: lexicographic vs numeric filter operators in PostgresStore
signals.review_reason: Silently incorrect query results in production — not a crash but a correctness bug that can cause wrong business decisions. Data passes filter when it shouldn't. SqliteStore already has correct implementation, confirming the bug.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: Numeric filter operators ($gte, $gt, $lt, $lte) silently return incorrect results using lexicographic ordering. A score=2 document incorrectly passes {"score": {"$gte": 10}}. SqliteStore already handles this correctly.

aliases: user types become dicts on checkpoint resume
signals.review_reason: Data corruption on resume is a significant workflow disruption — type information is silently lost, causing downstream code to receive dicts instead of typed objects. Blocks type-safe workflows.

source_issues.title: Honor allowed_msgpack_modules in langgraph.json

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite in the same batch
signals.summary: A guard `if not seen_overwrite:` prevents the operator from applying to values after an Overwrite in the same batch. In concurrent supersteps, if Task A writes Overwrite(base) and Task B writes a regular value, Task B's value is silently lost.
aliases: values silently dropped in concurrent supersteps
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in concurrent execution — state updates are silently dropped with no error or warning. This is a correctness bug that can cause agents to lose intermediate computation results.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: Values arriving after an Overwrite in the same batch are silently discarded due to `if not seen_overwrite:` guard. Race condition between concurrent supersteps causes data loss.

signals.topic: PostgresSaver.setup() fails with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside a transaction, breaking atomic provisioning flows
signals.summary: PostgresSaver.setup() raises psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction because CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. Affects users who need atomic provisioning where setup() should roll back together with sibling DDL.
aliases: PostgresSaver atomic setup fails in transaction
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in transaction block
signals.review_reason: Breaks atomic database provisioning — users cannot set up PostgresSaver within a transaction, forcing manual index creation or breaking rollback semantics. Real operational pain.

source_issues.title: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
source_issues.evidence: psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction error when PostgresSaver.setup() is called inside a transaction. Breaks atomic provisioning flows that need rollback to include setup().

signals.topic: TypeScript SDK v3 silently transforms user-defined metadata keys from snake_case to camelCase, breaking data round-trip

aliases: TS SDK metadata key case transformation data corruption
snake_to_camelKeys corrupts opaque user metadata fields

source_issues.title: [TypeScript SDK] v3 silently camelizes user-defined `metadata` keys on read, breaking round-trip
