Breaks RunStreamingAsync in any AGUI workflow with handoff.

signals.topic: .NET/Python: Multiline YAML block scalar syntax in SKILL.md frontmatter parsed incorrectly — captures only '|' or '>' character
signals.summary: Both .NET and Python skill loaders use regex that only matches single-line key-value pairs, so YAML block scalars (| or >) used for description fields are parsed as just the indicator character, breaking skill descriptions and compatibility metadata.
aliases: SKILL.md YAML block scalar parsing broken
YAML multiline description parsed as pipe character
signals.review_reason: Affects both .NET and Python runtimes for skill loading, a core framework feature. Skill descriptions are silently corrupted (only '|' is captured), making skills using multiline YAML effectively broken without clear error messages.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Multiline YAML descriptions not parsed correctly
source_issues.evidence: Both .NET (AgentFileSkillsSource.cs sYamlKeyValueRegex) and Python (_skills.py YAML_KV_RE) use single-line regex that captures '|' or '>' as the unquoted value instead of the indented multiline content. Root cause identified in both codebases. Affects description and compatibility fields.

signals.topic: Cannot configure custom OpenAI-compatible API endpoint through intermediate proxy
signals.summary: AutoGen only supports direct OpenAI library calls; users with custom intermediate endpoints (proxies, gateway, etc.) cannot use AutoGen, blocking their entire workflow.
aliases: Cannot route OpenAI calls through custom middleware
signals.review_reason: This is a direct workflow blocker: users with custom OpenAI-compatible API endpoints (proxies, API gateways, custom LLM backends) cannot use AutoGen at all. The user explicitly reports inability to complete their task, which qualifies as a key functionality limitation. Single-issue count due to file scope, but the impact is clear and structural (the library simply does not support custom endpoints in its current implementation).

source_issues.title: cant consume openai via requests
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'I am consuming an OpenAI instance via requests as i need to consume it using through an intermediate endpoint. Looks like the implementation of openai in autogen only supports direct calls using the library and i cant add my custom endpoint.' This directly blocks the user's main workflow.

signals.topic: MCP extension executablePath ignored: wrong browser/profile opened, MCP requests timeout
signals.summary: In @playwright/mcp extension mode, explicit --executable-path / PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH CLI flags are ignored. The extension opens the wrong browser (from channel fallback) instead of the specified executable. In WSL/CDE setups where the extension is installed in a mounted Windows Edge profile, this causes the extension to never connect and MCP requests to fail with timeout error -32001.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but related MCP extension regressions in 0.0.73 that together make the extension unusable: (1) browser dies between tool calls breaking AI agent workflows, (2) wrong browser opens ignoring explicit executable path causing MCP timeouts. Both have clear root causes and confirmed reproducible failures.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright MCP extension mode ignores explicit executable path
source_issues.evidence: In WSL/CDE setup, MCP with --executable-path pointing to Windows Edge profile opens Linux Edge instead. MCP requests timeout with error -32001. Root cause: CDPRelayServer created without passing executablePath, side effect of #40475.

source_issues.title: [Bug] @playwright/mcp 0.0.73 routes headed browser through launchApp — chromeless --app= window, dies between tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Since 0.0.73, headed MCP browser routing through launchApp loses toolbar/tabs/address bar (chromeless --app= mode injected). Browser dies between tool calls with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. MCP workflows with AI agents are completely broken.

signals.topic: WebKit headful mode fails with ProtocolError on Linux, blocking headed browser usage
signals.summary: WebKit headless mode is broken on Linux, causing `playwright.webkit.launch({ headless: false })` to throw a ProtocolError when initializing the session (Page.overrideUserPreference call fails with 'closed'). This makes headed WebKit completely unusable on Linux systems.
signals.review_reason: Core browser feature completely broken for WebKit on Linux — headed mode is a primary use case and throws ProtocolError immediately on page creation. Confirmed reproducible with minimal repro, affects all users on that platform.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: webkit does not work in headful mode
source_issues.evidence: Simple 3-line repro: launch WebKit headful, create page, goto URL. Throws ProtocolError 'closed' on Page.overrideUserPreference during session initialization. Affects all Linux Mint users.

signals.topic: WebKit on Debian12: 11 test failures due to IPv6 localhost resolution regression
signals.summary: A regression after commit a8ad57fc causes WebSocket connections to fail on Debian12 because localhost resolves to ::1 (IPv6) but WebKit's WebSocket only connects over IPv4 (127.0.0.1), resulting in ECONNREFUSED. Affects both browserType.connect and debug-controller functionality.
aliases: webkit debian12 ipv6 localhost websocket fail
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression with identified root cause (IPv6 localhost resolution). Blocks WebSocket-based features (connect, debug-controller) for all Debian12 WebKit users. Reproducible in CI environment, 11 test failures.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: 11 test failures on WebKit on Debian12 after a8ad57fcb4566146d4be6587c50bd7a095383ee4
source_issues.evidence: 11 test failures across browsertype-connect and debug-controller test suites, all with ECONNREFUSED to 127.0.0.1. Root cause identified: Debian12 defines localhost as ::1, and wsServer.ts defaults to 'localhost' which resolves to IPv6, but WebKit WebSocket only connects over IPv4. Proposed fix: change default hostname from 'localhost' to '127.0.0.1'.

signals.topic: Full-page screenshot renders iframe content as blank white
signals.summary: When taking a full-page screenshot on pages containing YouTube iframes, the iframe area is captured as a blank white rectangle instead of the actual rendered content. Viewport and per-element iframe screenshots work correctly, but full-page scrolling capture fails to composite iframe content.
signals.review_reason: Screenshot is a core debugging/verification feature. Capturing iframe content as blank defeats the purpose of full-page screenshots for any page using embedded content. Impact is high for visual testing and documentation workflows.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Full-page screenshot doesn't render iframe content
source_issues.evidence: Full-page screenshot captures YouTube iframe rectangle as blank white. Per-element iframe screenshot and viewport-after-scroll screenshot both render correctly. Reproducible with minimal repo at https://github.com/afonseca08/playwright-render-issue.

signals.topic: Firefox pointer events fail in parallel execution mode
signals.summary: When running multiple Playwright pages in parallel on Firefox, pointer events (hover, click, etc.) fail to trigger correctly — only one out of N parallel pages receives the pointer event. This makes parallel test execution fundamentally unreliable on Firefox, with users needing to fall back to serial execution.
signals.review_reason: Parallel test execution is a core performance feature. Pointer events failing in parallel on a major browser (Firefox) forces users to run tests serially, dramatically increasing test suite runtime. Reproducible with minimal repro, confirmed by multiple browser runs.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Pointer events don't work in Firefox in parallel
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro with 5 parallel pages on same browser, all hovering tooltips. Only 1 out of 5 pages receives the pointer event on each run. Same test always passes on Chromium/Safari. Previously reported in #27517 (closed for lack of bandwidth 2 years ago). Affects both headless and headed mode.

signals.topic: Handlebars/YAML prompt template plugins fail to execute when registered via DI — functions not called, returns error instead
signals.summary: When registering plugins via AddTransient/AddKeyedTransient in DI and using them in Handlebars/YAML prompt templates, the Kernel fails to invoke the registered functions, returning a 'cannot find the current user time' error instead of executing the plugin function.
aliases: Kernel.Invoke not calling registered plugin functions in Handlebars prompt template
Handlebars template plugin invocation fails with DI-registered plugins
signals.review_reason: DI-registered plugins silently fail to execute in Handlebars/YAML templates, returning an error instead of calling the function. This is a core workflow breakage: users following official DI patterns cannot use plugins inside prompt templates. Workaround requires abandoning the DI registration pattern entirely. Severity P1 due to complete feature blockage for this common integration pattern.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Kernel.Invoke Function is not calling other functions specified in the prompt template
source_issues.evidence: Plugin functions (e.g., TimePlugin.get_time) registered via DI are not invoked when used in Handlebars/YAML prompt templates. The kernel returns 'cannot find the current user time' instead of calling the function. User provided full reproduction code with DI registration and YAML template. 5 comments confirming the issue. Status: open, stale.

signals.topic: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync throws 'NOT NULL constraint failed' — vector upsert completely broken
signals.summary: Calling UpsertAsync on a SqliteVectorStore collection throws 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json' because the connector serializes non-vector properties into null/empty, violating the NOT NULL column constraint.
aliases: SqliteVectorStore NOT NULL constraint failed during upsert
SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync fails with NOT NULL constraint on json column
signals.review_reason: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync is completely broken — every upsert operation throws a SQLite constraint error. This blocks the entire vector upsert workflow for SQLite users. The bug is reproducible with a minimal record definition, and workarounds (explicit values, schema relaxation) do not resolve it. Only manual SQL bypasses the bug. Severity P1 due to complete blockage of a primary data operation.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: [SqliteVectorStore] NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json during UpsertAsync
source_issues.evidence: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync fails with 'NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json'. The json column is defined as NOT NULL but the connector serializes non-vector properties into null/empty. User provided a complete minimal reproduction with VectorStoreRecord attributes. Multiple workarounds tried (explicit non-empty strings, relaxed schema) — all failed. Manual raw SQL insert works, confirming the bug is in the connector. 5 comments. Status: open, stale.

signals.topic: Handlebars template execution_settings (max_tokens, temperature) completely ignored when PromptExecutionSettings object with ServiceId is passed
signals.summary: When creating a KernelFunction from a Handlebars prompt that includes an execution_settings block, providing a PromptExecutionSettings object (even with only a ServiceId) during function creation causes all template-defined settings (max_tokens, temperature, etc.) to be silently ignored.
aliases: Handlebars template execution settings ignored when PromptExecutionSettings is passed
PromptExecutionSettings with ServiceId overrides template settings incorrectly
signals.review_reason: This bug forces users to choose between dynamic ServiceId selection (losing template-defined settings) or hardcoding everything (losing flexibility). It fundamentally breaks the documented pattern of combining template defaults with runtime ServiceId selection. The defect is observable: output length confirms max_tokens was ignored. The only workaround (passing null) eliminates the ability to switch models at runtime — a significant functional regression.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: .Net: Handlebars Template execution_settings Ignored When Passing PromptExecutionSettings with ServiceId
source_issues.evidence: When PromptExecutionSettings (containing only a ServiceId) is passed to CreateFunctionFromPrompt with a Handlebars template that defines execution_settings (max_tokens=10, temperature=1.0), all template settings are silently ignored. The only workaround is to pass null for executionSettings, which prevents dynamic ServiceId selection. 4 comments. Full reproduction code provided. Status: open, stale.

signals.topic: SK Logging throws NotSupportedException when logging MCP tool results with TextContent — breaks observability when using MCP servers
signals.summary: When SK logging is enabled and MCP server tools (exposed via AsKernelFunction) return results containing TextContent types, the logging pipeline throws a NotSupportedException due to missing JsonTypeInfo metadata, making SK logging unusable in MCP integration scenarios.
aliases: NotSupportedException on SK Logging with MCP tools
SK logging fails for TextContent types from MCP AsKernelFunction
signals.review_reason: SK logging is entirely broken for MCP tool interactions. Users must disable logging to use MCP servers, removing critical observability. While the LLM execution itself is unaffected, the inability to log MCP tool results is a significant degradation of the observability experience. The workaround (disable logging) is a real cost to users who depend on logging for debugging and monitoring.

source_issues.title: Bug: NotImplementedException on SK Logging
source_issues.evidence: When SK logging is enabled with MCP server tools (via ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore and AsKernelFunction()), logging function results throws NotSupportedException: 'JsonTypeInfo metadata for type Microsoft.Extensions.AI.TextContent was not provided'. The workaround is to disable SK logging entirely, which removes observibility for MCP tool interactions. Repro steps provided. Status: closed.

signals.topic: SK OpenApi plugin throws 'Method not found' after upgrading to SK 1.50 — upgrade breaks the plugin
signals.summary: After upgrading to Semantic Kernel 1.50, the Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.OpenApi package throws a runtime 'Method not found' exception on AIFunctionFactoryOptions.set_CreateInstance, making the OpenApi plugin completely unusable after any upgrade.
aliases: OpenApi plugin broken after SK 1.50 upgrade
AIFunctionFactoryOptions method not found in OpenApi plugin
signals.review_reason: Upgrading from SK 1.49 to 1.50 causes a complete breakage of the OpenApi plugin via a missing method error. This is a silent breaking change from a minor version bump, forcing users to either stay on an older version (missing security patches and features) or lose OpenApi plugin functionality. No workaround is documented. Severity P1 due to upgrade-induced complete breakage of a commonly-used plugin.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.OpenApi
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to SK 1.50, OpenApi plugin throws 'Method not found: Void Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunctionFactoryOptions.set_CreateInstance(System.Func3)'. The user states 'nothing changes but only upgraded to 1.50'. This is a breaking change from a minor version upgrade. Status: closed, stale. 3 comments.

signals.topic: Pro/Plus plan quota draining significantly faster than expected after GPT-5.5 launch

One user burned through a weekly Pro quota in 20 minutes, representing direct monetary loss. Meets P0: count>=2, clear financial impact, paid subscriber base.

source_issues.title: Weekly quota draining insanely fast

Issue 21066 shows 'Access is denied' preventing Node MCP from starting on Windows. Together they confirm a persistent Windows regression. Meets P0: main workflow blocking + count=2 + paid subscriber.

source_issues.title: Codex is not responding... CONSTANTLY.
source_issues.evidence: Pro $100/mo user on Windows 11 reports constant 'Codex is not responding' with hourglass. Explicitly states 'It is the only app on my computer that behaves this way' and 'newer versions don't fix it.'

source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 user: 'failed to execute Node: Access is denied' (Přístup byl odepřen). Browser Use fails before opening a tab because node_repl cannot start Node. Direct functional block on Windows.

signals.topic: Safety check false positives: legitimate code flagged as security risk, blocking work
signals.summary: Enterprise users repeatedly get flagged as security risks by Codex safety checks when working with legitimate code (e.g., public data collection for government agencies, cybersecurity research). The false positives interrupt core workflows and block users from performing their jobs.
signals.review_reason: 2 confirmed false-positive safety blocks affecting enterprise users performing legitimate work (government data collection, cybersecurity research). Each block interrupts core professional workflow. While safety systems may be working as designed, the user impact is clear: legitimate work is being blocked. P1 because it is workflow-disrupting but not necessarily preventing all use.

source_issues.title: False positive securyty ricsc
source_issues.evidence: CLI user getting false positive safety check with uploaded thread reference. Explicitly marked 'safety-check' label.

source_issues.title: Flagged for collecting laws and regulations
source_issues.evidence: Enterprise user states: 'I keep being flagged as a cyber security risk for collecting public data—often at the behest of state/federal government agencies.' This directly blocks legitimate government-requested research workflows.

signals.topic: Blank overlay covers Plugins and Skills UI at certain window widths/display scaling on macOS
signals.summary: On Codex Desktop for macOS with Intel Macs and specific display scaling settings, a blank overlay visually covers the Plugins and Skills areas at certain window widths, making these features inaccessible even though they technically exist beneath the invisible overlay.
aliases: Plugins Skills hidden by blank overlay
signals.review_reason: Clear UI regression on macOS where Plugins and Skills UI is covered by an invisible overlay at certain window widths. Users are blocked from accessing a core feature (plugins/skills) due to a rendering/layout bug. One confirmed user with clear evidence (screenshot referenced). P1: key feature inaccessible, rendering bug confirmed.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop: blank overlay covers Plugins and Skills at certain window widths/display scaling on macOS
source_issues.evidence: Intel Mac with specific display scaling. Blank overlay visually covers Plugins/Skills UI at certain window widths. User cannot interact with those UI areas even though functionality exists underneath. Includes screenshot evidence referenced in issue.

signals.topic: Pet overlay opens but pet mascot is not visible to user
signals.summary: When users invoke the /pet command in Codex Desktop on macOS, the overlay/tray opens correctly but the pet mascot graphic itself is not rendered, leaving users with a blank/empty pet overlay despite the feature being technically active.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed rendering bug where pet mascot graphic fails to display while the overlay framework itself functions. One user with screenshot evidence. Not workflow-blocking but degrades a differentiating feature. P2: count=1, cosmetic-ish but confirmed rendering failure.

source_issues.title: /pet opens overlay/status tray but no pet mascot is visible
source_issues.evidence: User on macOS Apple Silicon runs /pet in Codex Desktop — overlay opens but no pet/avatar graphic is visible. Screenshot evidence provided showing empty overlay area where mascot should render.

signals.topic: Session compaction data loss: clear-then-add race causes permanent history deletion
signals.summary: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession.run_compaction() deletes session history before writing compacted replacement items; if add_items() fails after clear_session() succeeds, data is permanently lost. Affects SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr, SQLAlchemy, and custom Session backends.
signals.review_reason: P0 justified: clear data durability failure in session compaction, non-atomic clear-then-write pattern guaranteed to lose history on transient write failures across all persistent session backends. Direct user impact is permanent data loss — no recovery possible.

source_issues.title: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession can lose session history if add_items fails after clear
source_issues.evidence: clear_session() succeeds and add_items() fails → original session history already deleted. No atomic replacement. Affects all persistent session backends (SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr, SQLAlchemy). Reproducer confirms data loss scenario.

signals.topic: Sensitive data leakage: MCP invalid JSON errors expose raw tool input despite DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA flag
signals.summary: MCPUtil.invoke_mcp_tool() still includes raw malformed input_json in the ModelBehaviorError string even when DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA is enabled. Malformed MCP tool arguments leak tokens, cookies, internal URLs, and PII through exception strings that end up in application logs, traces, and alerting systems.
signals.review_reason: P1: Sensitive data in exception strings propagates to logs/traces despite explicit user opt-out. MCP inputs commonly carry tokens and PII. While single issue, user impact is direct data exfiltration through the error path — the flag is explicitly set to prevent this and it is bypassed.

source_issues.title: MCP invalid JSON errors still include raw tool input when DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly opt-out of tool data logging via DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA, pass malformed JSON with secret token, error string still contains '{"secret":"SECRET_TOKEN_123"'. Exception strings commonly propagate to logs, traces, and alerting systems.

signals.topic: Sensitive data leakage: function tool trace errors bypass trace_include_sensitive_data=False
signals.summary: Function tool failures attach raw exception messages to trace spans even when RunConfig(trace_include_sensitive_data=False) is set. If a function tool throws an exception containing an API key, SQL query, PII, or tenant data, that text is exported in trace error data despite the explicit privacy opt-out.
signals.review_reason: P1: Explicit privacy flag is bypassed, raw exception text containing secrets/PII leaks into trace exports. While single issue, this defeats a user-facing privacy control that other tool types correctly respect.

source_issues.title: Function tool trace errors ignore trace_include_sensitive_data=False
source_issues.evidence: RunConfig(trace_include_sensitive_data=False) is explicitly set; _run_single_tool() catches exceptions and calls attach_error_to_current_span() with raw str(e). Other tool paths (computer, shell) already use get_trace_tool_error() to redact. Reproducer confirms raw exception text leaks into trace export.

signals.topic: Session retry data loss: rewind_session_items deletes unrelated tail items beyond retry scope
signals.summary: rewind_session_items() pops session records before confirming the tail matches the target suffix, and in the server_tracker path keeps popping until a known server item is found — silently erasing unrelated items added by other runs or actors. Especially dangerous for shared or externally-updated sessions.
signals.review_reason: P1: Silent, non-atomic session history deletion that can erase items added by other runs. Particularly severe for shared/external sessions where retry cleanup silently destroys unrelated history with no user-facing error.

source_issues.title: rewind_session_items can delete unrelated tail session items during retry cleanup
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer with [known_server_item, unrelated_new_item, target_item] after rewind: result is [] — unrelated_new_item and known_server_item also deleted. Silent deletion of external/shared session history with no user notification.

signals.topic: Shell command corruption: coerce_shell_call splits string commands into individual characters
signals.summary: coerce_shell_call() treats a string-valued commands payload as a generic Sequence, so 'echo hi' is normalized into ['e','c','h','o',' ','h','i']. This corrupts shell execution and pollutes approval/audit behavior with character-level commands.
signals.review_reason: P1: Shell tool main execution path is corrupted by a type-checking bug that causes wrong behavior (character-level commands) with no error. Audit/approval flows see corrupted data. Direct runtime impact on a core feature.

source_issues.title: coerce_shell_call splits string commands into character lists
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer passes {'commands': 'echo hi'} → output is ['e','c','h','o',' ','h','i']. str is a Sequence in Python, causing unexpected character-level iteration. Shell execution semantics are corrupted.

signals.topic: Responses stream accumulator crashes with AttributeError when event item is None
signals.summary: response.output_item.added streaming event with item=None causes AttributeError in the SDK's internal accumulator, crashing the client before app-level code can handle it. Affects users of OpenAI-compatible custom providers.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：SDK内部累加器硬崩溃，应用程序无法恢复。影响所有使用自定义OpenAI兼容provider的用户，当provider发出item=None的流事件时客户端立即崩溃。

source_issues.title: Responses stream accumulator crashes when response.output_item.added has item=None
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type' — crashes inside SDK stream accumulator before application code can recover

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely when file status stuck at in_progress

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() never returns; vector_store_file.status=='in_progress' indefinitely; last_error is None; raw_file.status=='processed'. No timeout, no error, no escape.

unbounded pydantic schema rebuild memory leak
signals.review_reason: 显著成本损失：长时间运行的服务内存无限增长直至OOM。Pydantic SchemaValidator（重型Rust对象）每次parse()调用都被重复分配且永不释放。明确的生产服务崩溃场景。

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph provided; RSS grows linearly with request count in long-running server; OOM is the eventual outcome; TextFormatT TypeVar causes model_rebuild cache miss on every call

source_issues.title: Realtime does not execute tool calls with mcp

signals.topic: OAuth login loop — JWT not persisted to localStorage after GitHub OAuth callback
signals.summary: GitHub OAuth sign-in completes the server-side token exchange but JWT/refresh token are never written to clawhub.ai localStorage, trapping all new users in a sign-in loop. No user can authenticate.
signals.review_reason: Complete auth flow failure — every new user is blocked from registering. This is a primary user journey (sign-up) failure with concrete evidence: PKCE verifier persists but JWT/refresh token are missing, and the OAuth round-trip completes without error. The issue explicitly states 'Blocks all new sign-ups. No user can authenticate → no skill submission, no badges, no profile.'

source_issues.title: OAuth sign-in loop: Convex Auth callback succeeds but JWT never reaches clawhub.ai localStorage
source_issues.evidence: User cannot authenticate via GitHub OAuth. PKCE verifier accumulates in localStorage without cleanup. JWT and refresh token are both absent after the callback redirect. Blocks all new sign-ups — no user can authenticate, submit skills, earn badges, or access profile.

signals.topic: Same-owner package publish fails with 'Package already exists and belongs to another publisher' ConvexError
signals.summary: Package owners cannot publish new versions to their own packages — the backend rejects same-owner updates with a ConvexError even though the logged-in account matches the package's Owner field per inspect.
signals.review_reason: Main publish workflow is completely blocked for the package owner despite correct auth and metadata. The issue is reproducible, affects the biggest plugin's install path, and blocks users from receiving the latest version via the normal clawhub install mechanism. Two different auth methods (CI token + browser token) fail identically, confirming server-side bug rather than credential issue.

source_issues.title: ConvexError: Package already exists and belongs to another publisher — same-owner publish blocked on existing code-plugin (2026-05-04)
source_issues.evidence: Package @axonflow/openclaw v2.1.0 publish fails with ConvexError even though Owner field matches logged-in @saurabhjain1592. Both CI service token and manual browser-flow token fail identically. Last successful publish was v2.0.8 on 2026-05-02. Users running 'openclaw plugins install clawhub:@axonflow/openclaw' are blocked from v2.1.0. Impact: biggest plugin install path is broken.

signals.topic: Dashboard infinite crash loop — CONVEX Q(skills:listDashboardPaginated) Server Error
signals.summary: Opening the dashboard causes an infinite crash loop: the ErrorBoundary catches the Convex query error, remounts, and re-triggers the same failed query, flooding the console with sequential error IDs.
signals.review_reason: Dashboard — the primary logged-in experience — is completely unusable due to an infinite crash loop. The ErrorBoundary re-triggers the failed query on each remount, making the dashboard inaccessible for all users who visit /dashboard. This is a UX-blocking crash, not a graceful error state.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard crashes with CONVEX Q(skills:listDashboardPaginated) Server Error
source_issues.evidence: Dashboard never renders. Console floods with sequential error IDs from repeated failed Convex queries. ErrorBoundary catches and re-triggers the same query, causing an infinite loop. Users are left without access to the main dashboard UI where they manage their skills and stats.

signals.topic: Hosting deployment fails — CONVEX A(hosting/actions:deploy) Server Error with no recovery path
signals.summary: Users attempting to go live via ClawHub hosting receive a generic Server Error from the deploy action, with no guidance on cause or resolution. 4 comments suggest the issue persists and affects real users.
signals.review_reason: Hosting deployment is a primary ClawHub feature (going live) that is failing with a generic server error. 4 comment threads indicate the problem is ongoing and affects real users who cannot deploy. While only 1 issue, the error message provides no recovery path, making it a complete feature block for affected users.

source_issues.title: Couldn't go live
source_issues.evidence: User receives generic 'Something didn't work this time' error from hosting/actions:deploy. 4 comments on the issue indicate ongoing impact. The error is opaque — no specific error code, no recovery instructions provided to the user. Deployment is a core feature that is actively failing.

signals.topic: Onboarding white/light cards render unreadable text in dark mode (system foreground bleeds through, text becomes invisible)
signals.summary: Onboarding surfaces use hard-coded white backgrounds (#FFFFFF / #E8F4FD) with no explicit foreground, so in dark mode the system white foreground renders text invisible against the white background. This affects all onboarding cards across Welcome, Ready, Permissions, Connection, and Wizard pages — new users encounter unreadable blank screens during first-run.
aliases: white card foreground missing in dark theme
signals.review_reason: Users on dark mode encounter completely unreadable onboarding UI — white text on white background — during first-run, which is a primary entry point. This directly blocks the onboarding experience (P2 due to single-issue count, though impact is clear: new users cannot read the onboarding flow). PR #257 already confirmed the same root cause on yellow cards; white/blue cards are an identical unfixed recurrence.

source_issues.title: Onboarding: white/light cards render unreadable text in dark mode (PR 241 follow-up)
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed in PR #257 (yellow cards fixed). Same root cause (hard-coded #FFFFFF backgrounds with no explicit Foreground) affects all white cards across OnboardingCard.cs, WizardStepView.cs, PermissionsPage.cs, ConnectionPage.cs, ReadyPage.cs, WizardPage.cs, and blue info cards (#E8F4FD). Users on dark mode see white-on-white unreadable text during onboarding.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock credentials expire mid-gateway-life but are never refreshed — auth failure forces manual restart
signals.summary: After upgrading to v2026.5.3-1, the gateway caches AWS credentials from ~/.aws/credentials at startup. When credentials rotate (e.g. via mwinit/ada), all subsequent Bedrock calls fail with ExpiredTokenException until the gateway is manually restarted. The root cause is a regression where the SDK's fromIni() provider assumes credentials without an expiration timestamp are permanent, combined with a singleton BedrockClient holding stale credentials indefinitely. This is a core flow failure for all AWS Bedrock users on v2026.5.3+.
aliases: AWS credentials cache stale after rotation
credential refresh not working after upgrade
signals.review_reason: Auth failure that blocks all Bedrock calls after credential rotation, with regression evidence from prior working version. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover — this is a clear main-flow block for AWS Bedrock users on v2026.5.3+.

source_issues.title: Bedrock aws-sdk auth: ExpiredTokenException after credential file refresh (regression in v2026.5.3)
source_issues.evidence: All Bedrock calls fail with ExpiredTokenException after credentials rotate; only fix is restarting the gateway service. Regression from prior version where seamless credential refresh worked. Failover decision logs 'surface_error reason=auth'.

signals.topic: Telegram DM inbound routing silently drops messages — agent never responds to direct messages
signals.summary: Inbound Telegram direct messages to the configured bot are received by the webhook but never forwarded to the agent for processing. Outbound DMs and topic group messages work correctly. The DM session exists in sessions.json but the inbound message does not trigger an agent turn. This is a complete inbound routing failure for the most common personal-use Telegram pattern.
aliases: Telegram DM not routing to agent
Telegram inbound DM session silent drop
DM messages received but agent never responds
signals.review_reason: Complete inbound message routing failure for Telegram DM — the primary personal-use channel. User sends a DM, gateway receives it, but agent never processes it. Multiple recovery attempts failed. This blocks the core use case of receiving agent responses via Telegram DM.

source_issues.title: Telegram DM session not routing inbound messages to agent
source_issues.evidence: Gateway webhook receives DM but agent never generates a response. Multiple attempted fixes (restart, session reset, webhook verification) all fail. Outbound DM and group routing work correctly; only inbound DM routing is broken.

signals.topic: Discord WebSocket gateway never reaches ready — inbound messages silently never dispatch
signals.summary: On v2026.5.2 and v2026.5.3, the Discord channel WebSocket handshake never completes. The bot logs 'awaiting gateway readiness' and then goes silent — no messageCreate events fire, so the agent never wakes for Discord messages. The bot self-reports 'connected' despite the handshake not finishing. This is a full inbound failure for the Discord channel on two consecutive releases.
aliases: Discord inbound messageCreate events not firing
Discord channel stuck at 'awaiting gateway readiness'
signals.review_reason: Full Discord inbound failure on two consecutive releases (v2026.5.2 and v2026.5.3). The bot reports connected but the WebSocket handshake never completes, silently dropping all inbound messages. Last known working version is v2026.3.24 — this is a significant regression blocking Discord channel users.

source_issues.title: Discord channel: gateway WebSocket never reaches `ready` on 2026.5.2 and 2026.5.3 — inbound `messageCreate` events never dispatch
source_issues.evidence: WebSocket gateway handshake stalls at 'awaiting gateway readiness' with no error or reconnect. Inbound messages never reach the agent. Bot self-reports 'connected' but no messageCreate events dispatch. Last working version was v2026.3.24. Workaround requires switching to polling at significant token/latency cost.

signals.topic: Agent bootstrap takes 3+ minutes per turn — interactive sessions impractical due to extreme latency
signals.summary: Every agent turn (including simple 'hi' messages) takes 3-5 minutes to start streaming on a clean install. Trace logs show core-plugin-tools (~73s), system-prompt (~45s), and stream-setup (~45s) as dominant costs on every single turn. The bottleneck is in plugin loading and prompt composition, not workspace file sizes. This makes interactive real-time sessions completely impractical.
aliases: Agent prep stages 3+ minutes per turn
signals.review_reason: Every agent turn takes 3-5 minutes, making real-time interactive sessions completely impractical. Prep stages (core-plugin-tools, system-prompt, stream-setup) total 188 seconds per turn including on trivial 'hi' messages. Event loop blocked for up to 162 seconds. This is a main-flow performance block that makes the tool unusable for its intended purpose. Strong user impact evidence with detailed trace logs, event loop metrics, and multiple failed mitigation attempts.

source_issues.title: Agent bootstrap takes 3+ minutes per turn; core-plugin-tools, system-prompt, stream-setup each 45-75s
source_issues.evidence: prep stages total 188,133ms per turn. Event loop blocked 60-160s at 100% CPU on one core. 'agent cleanup timed out' after every run. All mitigations attempted (cleared cache, removed antivirus, slimmed workspace files) had no effect. User declares the tool impractical for interactive sessions.

signals.topic: Windows: all media uploads fail with EPERM fsync error — files silently dropped on Telegram and Discord
signals.summary: On Windows, writeSavedMediaBuffer opens the temp file read-only and then calls fsync(), which requires GENERIC_WRITE on Windows. Every binary attachment sent via Telegram or Discord fails with EPERM, and the file is never delivered to the agent. This affects all Windows users on both telegram and discord channel plugins.
aliases: Windows EPERM fsync on read-only handle
media uploads silently fail on Windows
Windows image upload broken Telegram Discord
signals.review_reason: All media uploads on Windows silently fail for both Telegram and Discord channels. The file is never delivered to the agent — no error is surfaced to the user beyond gateway logs. This affects every Windows user sending attachments. The root cause is a clear code defect (read-only file handle used for fsync).

source_issues.title: writeSavedMediaBuffer fsyncs a read-only file handle → EPERM on Windows (drops all media uploads)
source_issues.evidence: Every Telegram and Discord binary attachment fails with EPERM fsync error. File never delivered to agent. Reproduced on Node 22.22.2 and 24.13.0, both telegram and discord channels. Windows FlushFileBuffers requires GENERIC_WRITE. User offers a PR with the fix.

signals.topic: LLM generates unintended files from markdown code blocks in README creation

markdown code blocks misinterpreted as file creation commands

signals.topic: OpenAI embeddings provider ignores passthrough props, blocking RAG dimension comparisons
signals.summary: The OpenAI embeddings provider does not forward passthrough parameters (e.g., 'dimensions') to the underlying API, unlike the responses provider. Users performing RAG pipeline evaluations with different embedding dimensions cannot control the parameter and must fall back to workarounds.
signals.review_reason: Issue #9098 describes a functional gap where the OpenAI embedding provider silently drops passthrough props, directly blocking RAG evaluation workflows that require configurable embedding dimensions. The user describes an explicit use case (comparing RAG performance across dimension settings) that cannot be achieved with current behavior. This is not merely a feature request — it is a missing capability that breaks a core evaluation scenario. Single-occurrence but with high user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Bug: OpenAI embeddings ignore passthrough
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states they cannot evaluate RAG pipeline with different dimension parameters because passthrough is ignored, forcing a workaround. The fix would be to either expose dimensions directly or forward passthrough like other providers do.

signals.topic: Claude Agent SDK provider returns incorrect output when background sub-agents emit result messages
signals.summary: The anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider exits its stream loop at the first result message, which for background sub-agents is not the main agent's final response. Users running evals with Claude Code-style background agents receive sub-agent summaries instead of the main agent's actual output, producing incorrect eval results.
aliases: Claude Agent SDK returns sub-agent result instead of main agent result
SDK provider early return on background agents
signals.review_reason: Issue #9054 is a confirmed bug (closed with fix suggested) where the Claude Agent SDK provider returns wrong output when background sub-agents are used. The user impact is clear: eval results are incorrect because the provider surfaces the sub-agent summary rather than the main agent's final response. This directly undermines the correctness of evaluations — a core use case — and was reproducible with a specific prompt pattern. Although only 1 issue, the severity is high: wrong eval outputs can lead to incorrect pass/fail decisions.

source_issues.title: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider returns early when background sub-agents emit result messages
source_issues.evidence: The provider's for-await loop (line 1024) hits the first result message and immediately returns, exiting before the main agent's terminal result arrives. Users running evals that spawn background sub-agents receive sub-agent summaries as the eval output instead of the main agent's final reply, making the eval results incorrect.

signals.topic: vLLM `best_of` parameter removed causes TypeError on every `.complete()` call, blocking LLM completions
signals.summary: vLLM >= 0.19.0 removed `best_of` from SamplingParams, but llama-index-llms-vllm hardcodes it in _model_kwargs, causing TypeError on every completion call.
signals.review_reason: vLLM completions are a core workflow — every completion call crashes with TypeError. This is a hard failure that completely blocks the vLLM LLM integration, qualifying as P0 despite count=1 due to absolute user impact (main flow blocked, no workaround).

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index-llms-vllm: best_of removed from vLLM SamplingParams causes TypeError on .complete()
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'best_of' thrown on every .complete() call. Hardcoded kwarg incompatible with vLLM >= 0.19.0.

signals.topic: Base64 encode returns bytes instead of string, causing downstream serialization crashes
signals.summary: base64.b64encode() returns bytes but the function casts it to str, causing runtime crashes when downstream code attempts to concatenate or JSON serialize the result.
aliases: base64 bytes str type mismatch serialization crash
signals.review_reason: Confirmed type mismatch that produces runtime crashes in downstream code that consumes base64 output. Not a warning — causes actual failures in serialization pipelines.

source_issues.title: fix: base64 encode returns bytes instead of string, causing serialization crashes
source_issues.evidence: base64.b64encode() returns bytes, function uses typing.cast(str, ...) which only satisfies type checker. Downstream concatenation or JSON serialization fails at runtime.

signals.topic: Ollama streaming silently drops thinking-only chunks, causing incomplete or truncated agent responses

signals.review_reason: Streaming is a core Ollama use case. Silent truncation of thinking content without user notification degrades the agent experience and can lead to incomplete responses reaching end users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: stream_chat / astream_chat in llama-index-llms-ollama drops thinking-only chunks
source_issues.evidence: Guard 'if r["message"]["content"] is None: continue' skips chunks where thinking is present but content is None. DeepSeek-R1 extended-thinking responses are silently truncated.

signals.topic: DashScope MultimodalEmbedding API response format changed, breaking embedding generation

signals.review_reason: External API breaking change causes MultimodalEmbedding to fail completely. All users of DashScope multimodal embeddings are affected, with no indication from the code that the API format has changed.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: DashScope DashScope MultimodalEmbedding embedding failed
source_issues.evidence: Code parses response.output['embedding'] but DashScope API now returns response.output['embeddings'][0]['embedding']. MultimodalEmbedding generation is broken for all DashScope users.

signals.topic: refresh_ref_docs() silently drops kwargs after first document in batch, corrupting update behavior

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `refresh_ref_docs()` / `arefresh_ref_docs()` drop kwargs after the first document in a batch

source_issues.title: 5 'real-implementations' features broken or cosmetic end-to-end (workers, embeddings, SONA, hive-mind, Tier 2 routing)

signals.topic: agentdb repack missing dist/utils/vector-math.js causes silent ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND breaking HierarchicalMemory
signals.summary: claude-flow's repacked agentdb ships with a malformed dist/ layout where dist/controllers/HierarchicalMemory.js imports '../utils/vector-math.js' but the file does not exist at that path (only at dist/src/utils/vector-math.js). This causes ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on any code path through HierarchicalMemory, breaking hierarchical memory consolidation silently (no crash, operations become no-ops or Bridge-not-available downstream).
aliases: silent module not found breaking memory consolidation
signals.review_reason: P1评级：打包错误导致HierarchicalMemory功能静默失效（非崩溃，操作为空操作）。虽然是静默失败而非显式阻断，但问题性质为关键内存功能不可用，且属于已知的重复性打包缺陷模式（#1343/#1471同类型），用户需要手动打补丁才能工作。

source_issues.title: claude-flow's repacked agentdb is missing dist/utils/vector-math.js — HierarchicalMemory.js silently ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with node -e import() call confirming ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; standalone agentdb package unaffected (only repack is broken); workaround is a manual file copy to populate missing path; filed by Megatron autonomous build agent with concrete repro steps; similar bug class to resolved issues #1343 and #1471 indicating a recurring packaging defect pattern.

signals.topic: WASM runtime SyntaxError in @ruvector/rvf-wasm@0.1.6 crashes memory init, hooks pretrain, status and other RVF-touching commands
signals.summary: The published @ruvector/rvf-wasm@0.1.6 mixes import.meta.url and export default in a CJS-classified file, causing SyntaxError in all Node.js consumers. Affects ruflo memory init, ruflo hooks pretrain, ruflo status, and any RVF-touching command. Reproduces on clean install. Workaround requires patching package.json to add 'type: module'.
signals.review_reason: P1评级：SyntaxError导致memory init、hooks pretrain、status等核心命令启动时崩溃。虽然是上游包问题，但影响ruflo的核心初始化路径，用户需要手动patch package.json才能运行。count=1不满足P0条件，但启动崩溃的严重性足以归为P1。

source_issues.title: ruflo memory init / hooks pretrain crash: SyntaxError in @ruvector/rvf-wasm@0.1.6
source_issues.evidence: Clean npm install -g ruflo@latest followed by ruflo init --full and ruflo memory init reproduces SyntaxError; workaround confirmed by author and requires sed patch on package.json; upstream issue tracked at ruvnet/RuVector#415; impacts core initialization workflows.

signals.topic: HNSW availability false negative: embeddings index status and performance benchmark report 'package missing' when package is actually present
signals.summary: ruflo embeddings index status and ruflo performance benchmark incorrectly report HNSW as unavailable and display misleading hint 'npm install @ruvector/core' — but the package is actually installed and loadable. The real cause is that neither codepath initializes the in-process HNSW index before checking its state. This creates false bug reports where users install the supposedly-missing package to no effect.
aliases: HNSW index not initialized false alarm
signals.review_reason: P2评级：HNSW可用性报告为假阴性，虽然错误信息具有误导性导致用户困惑，但不影响核心功能实际运行（hooks route等其他命令正常初始化HNSW）。属于用户体验下降而非功能阻断。

source_issues.title: embeddings/performance commands report 'HNSW unavailable' due to uninitialized in-process index, not missing package
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed @ruvector/core@0.1.31 IS installed and loads cleanly in Node; getHNSWStatus() checks module-local hnswIndex which starts null in fresh CLI invocations; asymmetry: hooks route and hooks intelligence stats initialize the index correctly and report it available; issue creates false bug-report loop per author.

signals.topic: Headless Chrome silently drops geolocation permission without pre-grant
signals.summary: session-setup launches Chrome headless but does not call CDP Browser.grantPermissions({permissions: ['geolocation']}) before navigation. Headless Chrome suppresses prompt UI, so pages calling navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition() fail silently with PERMISSION_DENIED or no callback. Users must manually set geo overrides before navigation as a non-obvious workaround.
signals.review_reason: Clear root cause identified: headless Chrome blocks geolocation silently because session-setup doesn't pre-grant permissions via CDP. Blocks core headless automation workflows that depend on location APIs. Workaround requires manual geo override which is non-obvious. While count=1, impact is a complete feature block for a common automation scenario.

source_issues.title: session-setup doesn't pre-grant geolocation; permission prompts skipped or silently fail
source_issues.evidence: Root cause explicitly identified: session-setup skips CDP Browser.grantPermissions before first navigation in headless mode. Headless Chrome suppresses geolocation prompt UI, blocking all pages that call getCurrentPosition(). Workaround exists but is non-obvious and requires knowing location ahead of time.

signals.topic: Chrome M136+ default profile blocks --auto-connect (DevToolsActivePort not created)
signals.summary: Chrome M136+ added security hardening that prevents binding the remote debugging port on user/default profiles. The DevToolsActivePort file is no longer created for default profiles, causing --auto-connect to silently fail or time out without any error message. Users must manually launch a separate Chrome instance with explicit --remote-debugging-port and --user-data-dir.
signals.review_reason: Complete main-flow blockage on the default Chrome profile (the most common usage). Silent failure with no error message. Affects all users with Chrome M136+ on their default profile, which is the dominant Chrome installation. Count=1 but review_reason provides strong evidence: primary use path broken silently for the majority of users.

source_issues.title: --auto-connect fails on Chrome M136+ default profile (DevToolsActivePort not created)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause explicitly identified: Chrome M136+ security tightening prevents DevToolsActivePort file creation on user/default profiles. --auto-connect silently fails or times out. Default profile is the most common Chrome profile, making this a main-flow blockage for all default-profile users upgrading to M136+.

signals.topic: CLI click command does not recognize @element-ref syntax from snapshot, shows misleading error
signals.summary: The CLI's click command doesn't recognize @ref element references produced by the snapshot command (e.g., @e16). Instead it parses @e16 as a positional argument, then reports 'Missing arguments for: click' because it expects a CSS selector. This breaks the documented quick-start workflow where users take a snapshot and then click elements by reference.

click command parse error element ref

signals.topic: trace stop and profiler stop cross-contaminate each other's CDP recorder state
signals.summary: Both trace and profiler commands use the same underlying CDP tracing state but the stop commands do not track which command started the recorder. profiler stop after trace start succeeds and consumes the trace; trace stop after profiler start succeeds and prevents profiler stop. Both produce confusing errors.
signals.review_reason: Clear bug with deterministic repro; both commands produce wrong behavior and wrong error messages. However, trace and profiler are specialized profiling features used by advanced users, not core automation primitives. Count=1 and not a main-flow blocker. P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: trace stop and profiler stop can stop the other recorder type
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic reproduction steps provided: trace start followed by profiler stop succeeds and consumes trace, then trace stop fails. Reverse order produces same cross-contamination. Both commands produce confusing errors and neither produces the expected artifact.

signals.topic: agent-browser doctor ignores executablePath config, reports false 'No Chrome binary found'
signals.summary: The doctor command ignores the executablePath setting from config.json. It only checks agent-browser cache, system Chrome, puppeteer cache, and playwright cache. A user with Edge configured via executablePath gets a false 'No Chrome binary found' failure from doctor, despite the `open` command working correctly because it reads the config.
signals.review_reason: doctor is a diagnostic tool that is supposed to help users identify setup issues. Actively misleads users with a false positive when executablePath is configured. Undermines trust in the tool's self-diagnostic capabilities. While count=1, the diagnostic mislead is a significant UX regression for non-default-browser users.

source_issues.title: `agent-browser doctor` does not respect `executablePath`
source_issues.evidence: User has executablePath set to Edge in config.json. doctor reports 'No Chrome binary found' and suggests 'agent-browser install'. Yet `agent-browser open example.com` works fine because it reads the config. doctor actively misleads users away from their working configuration.

signals.topic: Zod ≥4.4.x breaks Bedrock tool-use streaming — every tool call throws AI_TypeValidationError
signals.summary: After upgrading Zod to ≥4.4.0, BedrockToolUseSchema's `input: z.unknown()` field is now required rather than optional, causing every streaming tool-use event to fail validation with AI_TypeValidationError. This is a breaking change for all users who pin Zod ≥4.4.x with @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency (every tool call) + main flow blocking. Zod ≥4.4.x is a routine version bump that silently breaks all Bedrock tool-use streaming — a core AI SDK workflow. Workaround (pin to ^4.3.x or patch-package) is impractical for production teams. Two independent reports (#14892, #14930) confirm real-user impact.

source_issues.title: `BedrockToolUseSchema` rejects valid `contentBlockStart` events under Zod ≥ 4.4.0
source_issues.evidence: Every tool call made through @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock fails validation when the project resolves zod@>=4.4.0. Error reproducible with real Bedrock payload. Same payload passes under zod@4.3.6 and fails under zod@4.4.0. Workaround requires pinning zod to ^4.3.x or applying patch-package.

source_issues.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): BedrockToolUseSchema input field breaks with zod@4.4.x
source_issues.evidence: Bedrock's contentBlockStart streaming event for tool use sends toolUse without an input field. This worked with zod@4.3.x but zod@4.4.0 changed z.unknown() to reject missing keys. Fix: input: z.unknown().optional().

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google: streaming parser drops no-args function calls, causing thoughtSignature loss and 400 errors in multi-turn Gemini 3 conversations
signals.summary: When streamFunctionCallArguments is enabled and a model calls a tool with an empty input schema, the streaming parser drops the entire function-call chunk because none of the three classification buckets match. The thoughtSignature carried by that chunk is also lost. For Gemini 3 thinking models, Vertex enforces that every function-call turn must contain at least one thoughtSignature — dropping it causes the next agent step to return a 400 error.
aliases: Gemini 3 thoughtSignature dropped through AI Gateway
no-args tool call dropped by Google streaming parser
signals.review_reason: High-severity main flow blocker for agentic multi-turn conversations with Gemini 3. Vertex enforces thoughtSignature as a hard requirement — missing it causes the entire next agent step to 400. Reproducible on both direct @ai-sdk/google-vertex path and AI Gateway path with wire-level evidence. Two related reports (#14847, #14840) confirm the same root cause affecting production agent systems.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing thoughtSignature
source_issues.evidence: Wire-level evidence shows Vertex sends thoughtSignature on the first call but parser drops it. A no-args complete call arrives as { name: 'X' } with no args, no willContinue, no partialArgs — none of three classifiers match. Observed in ~50% of multi-turn conversations depending on model tool choice. Workaround: add required arg to every tool (impractical for existing projects).

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: providerMetadata.vertex.thoughtSignature dropped on tool-call events when routing to Vertex Gemini

signals.topic: embed() and embedMany() crash with TypeError when using EmbeddingModelV2 providers that omit the warnings field
signals.summary: EmbeddingModelV2 doEmbed return types do not include a warnings field, but the SDK embed code paths assume it is always defined. This causes TypeError crashes (Cannot read properties of undefined, result.warnings is not iterable) in the embed and embedMany main API paths.
aliases: embedMany TypeError result.warnings is not iterable
signals.review_reason: Main flow crash in the embed/embedMany APIs triggered by any v2-era embedding provider (e.g. older @ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.0.x) combined with a recent ai SDK — a realistic real-world combination. The crash occurs at runtime with no graceful degradation, blocking the embedding use case entirely for affected consumers. Reproduction steps and root cause locations confirmed.

source_issues.title: embed() and embedMany() crash with EmbeddingModelV2 providers that omit warnings
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length') at logWarnings and TypeError: result.warnings is not iterable at embedMany. Reproducible with MockEmbeddingModelV2. Affects any consumer pinning a v2-era provider package alongside a recent ai SDK. Root cause confirmed at three boundary sites in embed.ts and embed-many.ts propagating modelResponse.warnings without null guard.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/mcp: CallToolResultSchema rejects resource_link content parts with Zod ≥4.4.x, breaking MCP tool calls
signals.summary: CallToolResultSchema in @ai-sdk/mcp only accepts three content variants (TextContent, ImageContent, EmbeddedResource) but the MCP spec defines a fourth variant, resource_link. With Zod ~4.3.6 the missing union arm was tolerated as permissive passthrough; with Zod >=4.4.1 it is hard-rejected and the SDK throws 'Failed to parse server response' from callTool().
aliases: MCP tool result resource_link zod 4.4 breaking change
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker for MCP tool calls involving resource_link content. The same Zod ≥4.4.x semantic change pattern as the Bedrock issue — a routine dependency update silently breaks a core SDK feature. MCP users with Zod ≥4.4.x cannot complete tool calls that return resource_link parts, which is a valid MCP spec type. The workaround of pinning zod to 4.3.x is impractical.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/mcp: CallToolResultSchema rejects resource_link content parts with zod ≥ 4.4.x
source_issues.evidence: MCP server returns resource_link content type. With zod >= 4.4.1 the SDK throws 'Failed to parse server response' from callTool(). The peer-dep range ^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8 permits 4.4.x, so this surfaces on a routine pnpm update. Same Zod 4.4.x root cause pattern as #14892.

signals.topic: Turbo commands execute slowly with high-CPU tokio worker processes (regression from v2.9.3→v2.9.8)
signals.summary: Command execution latency increased dramatically after upgrading from turbo 2.9.3 to 2.9.8. Users observe multiple tokio-rt-worker processes consuming full CPU cores during normal turbo runs, causing commands that should take seconds to hang for minutes. A second independent report (#12693) confirms related high-CPU behavior in 2.9.7 under tmux, indicating a systemic performance regression in recent releases.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm a performance regression in recent turbo versions causing high CPU consumption and dramatically slowed command execution. Issue #12703 shows a direct repro (upgrade from 2.9.3→2.9.8 causes 'forever' hangs), and #12693 confirms related high-CPU child process spawning in 2.9.7 under tmux. This is a primary workflow runtime blocker — users' build/dev commands become unusable. Count=2 from two distinct issues.

signals.topic: Turbo silently scans entire home directory and hangs indefinitely when project lacks .git (e.g. ZIP download)
signals.summary: When a project downloaded as a ZIP lacks a .git folder, turbo walks up the filesystem tree to find a git root. If it finds .git in the user's home directory (from an unrelated repo), it treats home as the monorepo root and scans hundreds of thousands of files for gitignore/hashing — causing an indefinite silent hang with no error or warning output.
signals.review_reason: A single but extremely severe report describing a complete workflow block: turbo silently hangs with no output after printing the banner, consuming minutes to hours of CPU scanning the user's entire home directory. This is a primary workflow blocker with a confusing failure mode (no error message, just a blank terminal). While count=1, the severity and the wide range of affected users (anyone who downloads a project as ZIP) justify P0.

source_issues.title: Turbo silently scans entire home directory and hangs when project has no .git (ZIP download)
source_issues.evidence: Turbo resolves home dir as git root via git rev-parse --show-toplevel, then walks ~500k files with zero output. No warning, no error — process hangs indefinitely until killed. Confirmed on macOS with self-hosted Gitea ZIP downloads.

This blocks a core use case (pruned Docker builds with Bun). While count=1, the evidence is concrete (public minimal repro, exact error message) and the impact is a complete build failure.

source_issues.title: `turbo prune --docker` generates invalid Bun lockfile; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` fails in pruned Docker stage
source_issues.evidence: Docker build fails at RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'; root lockfile installs correctly with frozen flag; failure only occurs in pruned out/json/bun.lock; minimal public repro repo provided.

signals.topic: Cache miss after deleting build output files; turbo re-runs tasks instead of restoring from cache
signals.summary: When a user deletes the output directory of a built package (e.g., rm -r apps/nuxt/.output), turbo reports a cache miss on the next run and re-executes the build task, instead of recognizing the cached artifact still exists in .turbo/cache and restoring the outputs.
signals.review_reason: Turbo's cache behavior incorrectly treats output file deletion as a cache invalidation event, causing unnecessary task re-execution. This is a UX and performance degradation: the core value proposition of turbo is avoiding redundant work, but deleting build artifacts (a common developer action) breaks this guarantee. Count=1 but clearly reproducible.

source_issues.title: Cache miss after deleting output files
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible: first build, second build (FULL TURBO OK), delete output dir, third build (cache miss + rebuild). Windows user with pnpm9. Public repro repo provided.

signals.topic: VercelResponse TypeScript types advertise Express helpers (res.status/json/send) that are absent in Rust Node runtime, causing silent production 500 errors
signals.summary: The `@vercel/node` VercelResponse type declares Express-style helpers (res.status(), res.json(), res.send()) that are not attached to the response object at runtime in Vercel's Rust-based Node runtime. TypeScript compiles cleanly, but production deploys fail with 'TypeError: res.status is not a function' returning HTTP 500. This is a compile-time-pass / runtime-fail mismatch that only surfaces after deploy.
aliases: TypeScript runtime mismatch in Rust Node runtime
VercelResponse Express helpers missing in Rust runtime
tsc --noEmit passes but production throws res.status is not a function
signals.review_reason: This is a classic type-runtime mismatch user pain point. TypeScript types advertise Express helpers that don't exist at runtime in the Rust Node runtime, causing silent production 500 errors. Code compiles cleanly under tsc --noEmit, making this a sharp trap that only surfaces after deploy. Count=1 limits it to P1, but the user impact is severe (production outage) and the mechanism is well-evidenced.

source_issues.title: @vercel/node TypeScript types declare Express-style helpers (res.status, res.json) that are absent in the Rust Node runtime
source_issues.evidence: TypeScript compiles without error but production returns HTTP 500 with 'TypeError: res.status is not a function'. Stack trace shows '/opt/rust/nodejs.js'. Users following Express-style examples from older Vercel docs hit 500 on first deploy without a clear pointer to the cause.

signals.topic: vercel env add --sensitive --yes --value silently stores empty string instead of reporting an error
signals.summary: The combination of `--sensitive --yes --value` flags on `vercel env add` returns a success message and exit code 0, but the variable is stored with an empty value. This silently corrupts production environment variables. Diagnosed only after hours of confusion when 'vercel env pull' revealed length 0 despite 'vercel env ls' showing the variable as 'Encrypted'.
aliases: --sensitive flag silently corrupts env var saves
vercel env add silently saves empty value with --sensitive flag
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption of production environment variables is a critical user pain. The command reports success while storing an empty string, with no error or warning. The impact is production outages (HTTP 500 from misconfigured secrets) that are extremely difficult to diagnose because 'vercel env ls' shows the variable as 'Encrypted' (looks healthy). This is a high-severity workflow runtime issue meeting P0 criteria despite count=1, due to the clear and severe user impact evidence (hours of confusion, production break).

source_issues.title: vercel env add --value V --sensitive --yes silently saves empty string
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces consistently across CLI versions 50.42.0 and 51.6.1, both locally and in CI. The command returns 'Added Environment Variable' with exit 0 but the actual stored value is empty. 'vercel env ls' shows 'Encrypted' (looks healthy) while 'vercel env pull' reveals length 0. User spent hours diagnosing 'the var is set, why is the function 500ing?'

signals.topic: vercel env add preview --value --yes fails with git_branch_required in non-interactive mode despite CLI hint recommending that exact form
signals.summary: Running `vercel env add NAME preview --value <V> --yes` (the exact command the CLI's own 'next' hint suggests for 'Add to all Preview branches') fails non-interactively with 'git_branch_required'. The user asked to skip confirmation but is still prompted. Adding --force makes no difference. Workaround requires direct REST API calls.
aliases: vercel env add non-interactive mode broken for preview branches
CLI hint contradicts actual behavior for env add preview --yes
signals.review_reason: Non-interactive CLI fails at a workflow-critical command (env var management in preview/production) despite the CLI itself suggesting the exact command form. This blocks automation and CI/CD pipelines. The self-contradicting UX (hint recommends a command that it just rejected) is a distinct user experience failure. Count=1 limits to P1, but the automation/CI blocking nature elevates it.

source_issues.title: vercel env add NAME preview --value V --yes returns git_branch_required despite hint suggesting that exact form
source_issues.evidence: The CLI returns a JSON error with 'status': 'action_required', 'reason': 'git_branch_required', and includes a 'next' array with a command that is exactly the same command that just failed. This is a self-contradicting UX failure. The user must fall back to direct REST API calls to achieve the documented non-interactive behavior.

signals.topic: vercel build produces unexpected TypeScript errors that do not occur with tsc/tsup, breaking the build pipeline
signals.summary: Running `vercel build` produces TypeScript errors (TS2339: Property 'body' does not exist on type 'Response', and multiple drizzle-orm type issues) that are not reproducible with standard tsc or tsup. Vercel runs an additional transformation step after the user's build command that introduces type errors. Users must resort to 'as any' workarounds to bypass the issue.
aliases: vercel build TS errors with hono/turborepo/drizzle
build pipeline type errors not reproducible locally
vercel build additional transformation causes TS errors
signals.review_reason: Build pipeline divergence is a significant user pain. Code that compiles locally fails in the Vercel build step due to type resolution differences. This blocks deployment and forces users to add 'as any' workarounds that degrade type safety. The issue is well-documented with a specific reproduction repo and multiple affected code paths (hono, drizzle, orpc).

source_issues.title: vercel build TS errors (hono/turborepo/drizzle)
source_issues.evidence: Local tsc/tsup builds succeed cleanly. 'vercel build' runs the same package.json build command successfully but then applies additional transformation that causes TS errors. Multiple projects affected: hono Response.body type mismatch, drizzle-orm column types, orpc headers. User is forced to add 'as any' casts as a workaround.

signals.topic: Python function builds prefer uv.lock over requirements.txt, causing dev dependencies to be included and risking 250MB deployment limit exceeded
signals.summary: Vercel's Python build process prefers uv.lock over requirements.txt for dependency installation. Since uv.lock can include dev dependencies and extras, deploying Python functions may exceed the 250MB size limit for serverless functions. Users must manually manage requirements.txt to avoid deployment failures.
aliases: Python deployment size limit exceeded due to uv.lock including dev deps
uv.lock preference causes Python function bundle bloat
signals.review_reason: Deployment size limit violations are a real user pain for Python function users, particularly those using uv with dependency groups. The 250MB hard limit is a known constraint, and including unnecessary dev dependencies increases the risk of exceeding it. However, this is a single issue with a feature-request component (changing preference logic), and the impact is situational (only affects users with large dev dependency sets). Marked P2 due to count=1 and situational scope, but the deployment-blocking nature of the size limit makes it worth keeping.

source_issues.title: Prefer requirements.txt over uv.lock for Python function builds to avoid excess dev dependencies
source_issues.evidence: uv.lock files include dev dependencies and extras (uv dependency groups feature). Python serverless functions have a 250MB hard deployment limit. Including dev deps in the deployed bundle can cause the limit to be exceeded, blocking deployment. The issue proposes changing build logic to prefer requirements.txt over uv.lock when both are present.

signals.topic: AI feature (Agent tab / Edit Predictions) crashes, loses input, or is disabled by certain code patterns
signals.summary: The Agent tab loses typed user input on send (silent failure after connection drop), the AI chat crashes when a user denies a request and sends new instructions, and Edit Predictions are entirely disabled when the file contains git conflict marker patterns in comments/docstrings.
aliases: edit predictions disabled by conflict markers
signals.review_reason: Three distinct failure modes within the AI feature set: (1) agent tab silently drops user input on send after connection loss, (2) AI chat crashes when denying a request, and (3) Edit Predictions completely disabled by git conflict marker patterns in documentation strings. All three represent key AI features becoming unavailable or unreliable, directly degrading the core AI-native editor value proposition.

source_issues.title: Agent tab loses user input
source_issues.evidence: User types a long message, clicks send, message disappears silently. User must re-type the entire message. Triggers when Zed loses connection to underlying agent (e.g. after idle period).

source_issues.title: AI chat crashes after denying request and giving new instructions
source_issues.evidence: User clicks Esc to deny a Codex ACP request, then sends new instructions. Chat UI disappears and shows an error footer. Direct crash of the AI chat feature.

source_issues.title: Edit Predictions disabled when code contains >>>>>>> UPDATED pattern in comments/strings
source_issues.evidence: Simply having git conflict marker text (<<<<<< CURRENT ... >>>>>> UPDATED) in a docstring or comment disables Edit Predictions for the entire buffer. Users writing documentation about git workflows are affected.

signals.topic: Debugger: startDebugging reverse request terminates parent session for forking apps (gunicorn, debugpy)
signals.summary: When debugging a forking Python app (e.g. gunicorn), Zed's DAP handler incorrectly sends terminate to the parent session after acknowledging a startDebugging reverse request, killing the master process and ending the entire debug session.
signals.review_reason: Blocks core debugging workflow for all forking Python apps (gunicorn, debugpy, celery, etc.) — the entire session is SIGKILLed instead of spawning a child debug session. Clear DAP trace evidence, root cause identified, and VSCode provides a working reference. High user impact: a developer cannot debug their production-like local dev environment at all.

source_issues.title: Debugger: startDebugging reverse request terminates parent session instead of spawning child session (breaks gunicorn --reload and other forking apps)
source_issues.evidence: DAP trace confirms Zed ACKs startDebugging correctly then immediately sends terminate to parent session. Exit code 247 (SIGKILL) received. Root cause: handler tears down parent instead of keeping it alive and opening a sibling child session. VSCode handles the same scenario correctly.

signals.topic: Copilot login for Edit Predictions fails with 'os error 32' (broken pipe), blocking the feature
signals.summary: When attempting to sign in to GitHub Copilot from Edit Predictions settings, the LSP connection is immediately broken (os error 32 / broken pipe), preventing Copilot from being used for edit predictions.
signals.review_reason: Copilot login failure completely blocks the Edit Predictions feature from working. The LSP immediately terminates with a broken pipe on initialization. This is a regression of a previously-fixed issue (#36093). Users cannot use Copilot for edit predictions at all — key feature unavailable.

source_issues.title: Cannot log in to Copilot for Edit predictions
source_issues.evidence: Log shows 'ERROR [lsp] cannot read LSP message headers', 'Server reset connection for initialize request', 'Broken pipe (os error 32)', 'copilot hasn't started yet'. Previously seen in #36093 (same broken pipe error, different Zed version) — regression of a known issue.

source_issues.title: Copilot login broken pipe (historical)
source_issues.evidence: Historical: same os error 32 broken pipe on copilot LSP startup, fixed by a prior update. Current issue is a regression.

signals.topic: Zed file cache overwrites on-disk changes when project folder is moved, causing permanent data loss
signals.summary: When a project folder is manually moved on the filesystem and reopened in Zed, the cached file versions overwrite the disk content, permanently losing edits made after the move.
aliases: file cache data loss on folder move
signals.review_reason: Permanent data loss caused by Zed's file cache overwriting disk content when a project folder is relocated. User explicitly reports losing 'several hours of work'. This is a catastrophic failure — file content is destroyed with no recovery mechanism. Blocks the fundamental editor guarantee of preserving user work.

source_issues.title: Zed's cache is corrupting project files.
source_issues.evidence: User moved project folder to new location, reopened in Zed, edited files and saved, closed project, moved folder back, reopened — cached versions overwrote disk content. 'several hours of my work have been lost'. No workaround available. Data loss is permanent.

signals.topic: macOS 'Fill From Messages' one-time code dialog blocks all terminal input until dismissed
signals.summary: On macOS, when the system 'Fill From Messages' dialog appears (for SMS 2FA codes), it prevents any interaction with Zed's built-in terminal, rendering the terminal unusable until the dialog is manually dismissed.
signals.review_reason: Terminal is a core feature of Zed as an IDE. When the macOS Messages autofill dialog appears (triggered by receiving an SMS 2FA code), all terminal input is blocked until the user manually dismisses the dialog. This is a main-flow failure for any developer who receives SMS codes while working — a common real-world scenario for developers with 2FA on their deployment tools.

source_issues.title: Can't use terminal if 'Fill From Messages' dialog appears
source_issues.evidence: Whenever the user receives a one-time code via SMS, the macOS 'Fill From Messages' autofill dialog appears and blocks all terminal input until clicked. User reports: 'will not allow me to do anything in the terminal until I click the fill. This is extremely annoying.'
